nodes.description: The Chambers Brothers were a criminal organization based in Detroit, Michigan, that dominated crack cocaine distribution in the city during the mid-1980s. Founded by four brothers from Marianna, Arkansas, the gang controlled over 50% of Detroit's crack trade, operating around 700 crack houses and generating $3 million daily. They were dismantled after a joint DEA and Detroit Police investigation led to their arrest in 1988 and conviction in 1989.

Bolivian criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking and human trafficking, operating in the Chapare region. It emerged from the merger of six coca growers' federations in the Chapare region, with origins dating back to 1964. The cartel is alleged to have strong connections with the Movement for Socialism political party and former president Evo Morales. Its current structure is unknown.

nodes.description: French far-right anti-Arab militant group active from 1973 to 1987. Formed by veterans of the Organisation armée secrète, it targeted Algerian properties, businesses, and government offices in France. The group claimed responsibility for several bombings, including the 1973 Algerian consulate bombing in Marseille. Its status is inactive, with no members ever arrested.

country_links.evidence_quote: Their attacks were primarily centered on Algerian properties, businesses, and government offices.
country_links.context: The group attacked Algerian properties, businesses, and government offices in France, targeting Algerian interests.

nodes.description: Irish American organized crime gang based in Charlestown, Boston, headed by the McLaughlin brothers. Active from the 1950s until 1966, the gang controlled gambling and loan sharking on the docks and carried out contract killings for the Patriarca and Genovese crime families. They were destroyed in a gang war with the Winter Hill Gang, resulting in the deaths or imprisonment of its leaders.

The Charlton Street Gang was a group of river pirates active on the Hudson River in New York City during the mid-19th century. They raided small cargo ships and later moved upriver, stealing a sloop in 1869 under leader Sadie the Goat. The gang engaged in kidnapping for ransom and flew the Jolly Roger flag. They dissolved by the end of the 1860s after conflicts with vigilantes.

One of the largest ethnic organized crime groups in the former Soviet Union, based in the North Caucasus and Moscow. Founded in the 1980s by Nikolay Suleimanov, it uses Chechen tribal structures (teip) and the abrek concept. Active in money laundering, racketeering, arms and drug trafficking, and cybercrime, with ties to Chechen separatism. Still active as of the present.

Chinese secret society established in 1880, with roots in 18th-century Fujian, China. It promoted Chinese values, customs, and democracy, and supported Sun Yat-sen's revolution. The organization spread to the United States and Canada, with headquarters in San Francisco. It remains active today.

nodes.description: Organised crime group based in Cheetham, Manchester, England, established by the early 1980s. Engaged in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, armed robbery, and other crimes. Known for turf wars with Moss Side and Salford gangs, and for controlling Manchester's club scene. At its peak between the late 1980s and early 2000s, still active as of present.

The Cherry Hill Gang was a New York street gang formed in the 1890s, known as the 'dandies' of the underworld for their dress suits and metal-weighted walking sticks. They robbed wealthy victims and were considered the most vicious gang in the city by the early 20th century. Their main rivals were the Whyos, and internal feuds led to sub-gangs forming.

Mexican drug cartel active in Chiapas and Guatemala, founded in 2022 as a splinter group of the Sinaloa Cartel. It emerged after a power struggle and defection to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. The group is involved in drug trafficking across the Guatemala-Mexico border and has published execution videos. Its founder was killed in 2025.

nodes.description: The Chichesters were an Irish-American street gang based in the Five Points area of New York City, founded by John Chichester in the 1820s. nodes.description: The Clan Abbinante is a Camorra organization operating in the northern area of Naples, specifically in the municipality of Marano di Napoli. Founded by Raffaele Abbinante, it was originally affiliated with the Nuvoletta clan and later became a trusted group of Paolo Di Lauro. The clan is involved in drug trafficking and cigarette smuggling, and has been engaged in violent feuds with rival clans. Key members include Raffaele, Guido, and Antonio Abbinante.

The Alfieri clan was a Camorra syndicate operating in the northeastern suburbs of Naples, specifically in the Saviano and Nola areas, with its stronghold in Piazzolla di Nola. Founded in 1953 by brothers Salvatore and Carmine Alfieri after their father's murder, it became part of the Nuova Famiglia confederation in the late 1970s to oppose Raffaele Cutolo's NCO. The clan played a key role in the war against the NCO, leading to Cutolo's defeat. Carmine Alfieri, known as 'o ntufato, led the clan after Salvatore's assassination in 1981.

The Clan Ascione is a Camorra organization originating and operating in the Ercolano area of Italy. It emerged in the 1980s, defeating the Esposito clan in a local feud. The clan is involved in racketeering and other criminal activities. Its current status is unclear from the text.

nodes.description: The Clan Cappello is a Mafia organization and family originating from the province of Catania, Sicily, named after boss Salvatore Cappello. It is considered, together with the Catania family of Nitto Santapaola, the most powerful Mafia clan in eastern Sicily. The clan emerged from the earlier Ferlito-Pillera group and rose to prominence in the 1980s under Salvatore Cappello.

Italian criminal organization based in Bari, active since the 1980s. Historically led by Antonio 'Tonino' Capriati, it is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and gambling. The clan is known for the prominent role of women in its operations. It operates mainly in Bari Vecchia and surrounding areas.

The Clan Cava is a Camorra organization based in Quindici, province of Avellino, Italy. It has been involved in a bloody feud with the rival Graziano clan for over thirty years. The clan operates in the Vallo di Lauro, Baianese, Nolano, and other areas of Campania, engaging in extortion, contract rigging, usury, and drug trafficking. Despite state crackdowns, it remains one of the most influential clans in the province of Avellino.

nodes.description: The Clan Cesarano is a Camorra organization originating from Ponte Persica, a hamlet northeast of Castellammare di Stabia, Italy, and operating there with strong interests and hegemony also in the neighboring municipality of Pompei. Founded by Ferdinando Cesarano, a charismatic figure in the Campanian organized crime scene of the late 1970s and early 1980s, the clan was initially part of the Nuova Famiglia before becoming independent in the mid-1980s. The clan is currently led by Luigi Di Martino, known as 'O Profeta, since 2014.

nodes.description: Camorra clan operating in the southern province of Naples, Italy, particularly in Castellammare di Stabia and the Scanzano district. Founded in the mid-1970s, it is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, and murder. The clan has alliances with other Camorra and 'Ndrangheta groups and has expanded into Emilia-Romagna.

Camorra clan operating in the eastern suburbs of Naples, specifically Ponticelli and Cercola. Founded by Antonio De Luca Bossa, known as 'o sicco, born in 1971. The clan was hostile to the Fusco-Ponticelli and Sarno clans, engaging in a bloody war for territorial control. After the arrest of its founder and the killing of his successor Giuseppe Mignano, the clan was eliminated by the Sarno clan.

Mafia clan originating from Barcellona Pozzo di Gotto, Sicily. Active since the second half of the 20th century, it was involved in the 1986 maxi-trial in Messina. The clan's structure is described as chaotic with shifting alliances, and it has connections with other mafia groups including the Santapaola family of Catania and Calabrian and Neapolitan organizations.

The Clan dei Casalesi is one of the most powerful Camorra clans and criminal organizations in Italy. It was created by Antonio Bardellino and originated in the municipalities of San Cipriano d'Aversa and Casal di Principe in the second half of the 20th century. The clan is active in Spain, Switzerland, and Romania, involved in cocaine trafficking, prostitution, construction, and money laundering.

The clan controls various illegal activities in Rome and Lazio, with ties to the Banda della Magliana. It remains active today.

nodes.description: The Clan dei catanesi was the Turin branch of the Catania-based Cursoti clan, active in the 1970s and early 1980s. It controlled gambling, prostitution, and heroin trafficking in Turin, supplied by the Milanese band of Angelo Epaminonda. The clan was dismantled by mass arrests in 1984 following the collaboration of several members, including boss Francesco Miano.

The Clan dei Corleonesi was a faction within Cosa Nostra formed in the 1970s, led by bosses from Corleone such as Luciano Liggio, Salvatore Riina, Bernardo Provenzano, and Leoluca Bagarella. It opposed the Palermo faction during the Second Mafia War in the early 1980s, eventually taking over the organization and initiating a period of attacks against the Italian state. The faction included mafia representatives from other provinces, like Nitto Santapaola and Francesco Messina Denaro.

Italian criminal organization originating from the Antico Corso area of Catania, Sicily. Active since the 1970s, it operated in northern Italy, especially Milan and Turin. The clan is divided into two factions, historically in conflict: the Milanese faction and the Catania faction. It was formed to counter the power of the Catania Mafia families led by Giuseppe Calderone and Benedetto Santapaola.

Italian-French criminal organization founded in Rome in 1973, operating between France and Italy during the early 1970s. Engaged in drug trafficking and lucrative kidnappings, becoming the first organized crime group to exert territorial control in Rome. It was composed of French ex-convicts from the Marseille milieu, linked to the French Connection.

It is considered the largest, most dangerous, and best-structured criminal group in Colombia, involved in drug trafficking, massacres, extortion, kidnapping, and other crimes. The group operates in hundreds of municipalities across Colombia and has an estimated 9,000 to 14,000 members. Its former leader Dairo Antonio Úsuga David (alias Otoniel) was captured in October 2021.

nodes.description: The Di Biasi clan, also known as 'i Faiano', was a Camorra organization operating in the Quartieri Spagnoli area of Naples, Italy. It emerged in the 1980s as a longa manus of the Giuliano clan. The clan was involved in drug trafficking and had a violent rivalry with the Russo clan, leading to multiple murders. In July 2008, a major police operation led to the arrest of several members, and the clan is now considered defunct.

Italian criminal organization based in Bari, founded in the 1980s by Antonio Di Cosola. Operates in the Carbonara, Ceglie del Campo, and Loseto neighborhoods. Involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and weapons possession. Weakened after the boss's collaboration with authorities.

The Clan Di Lauro is a Camorra organization based in the northern neighborhoods of Naples, Italy, founded by Paolo Di Lauro in 1982. At its peak in the 1990s and early 2000s, it earned over €500,000 daily from drug sales, making Secondigliano the largest open-air drug market in Europe. The clan was involved in a violent internal feud in 2004, leading to the Scissionisti di Secondigliano split. Its power declined after the arrest of Paolo Di Lauro in 2005.

nodes.description: The Fabbrocino clan is a Camorra mafia-type criminal organization originating from the area between Ottaviano, San Gennaro Vesuviano, and San Giuseppe Vesuviano in Italy. It was founded by Mario Fabbrocino after breaking away from Michele Zaza's group. The clan controls a vast territory in the Vesuvian area and is involved in diverse criminal activities including extortion, vote-buying, and money laundering through legitimate businesses. Mario Fabbrocino was sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of Roberto Cutolo.

country_links.evidence_quote: Mario Fabbrocino fu arrestato a San Martin, trenta chilometri circa da Buenos Aires , in Argentina , i primi di settembre 1997 .

nodes.description: The Clan Galasso di Poggiomarino was a Camorra organization operating in the hinterland east of Naples, based in Poggiomarino. Led by Pasquale Galasso and his brother Martino, it was considered one of the most powerful and ferocious clans in Camorra history, controlling neighboring municipalities and most public contracts in the province of Naples. The clan declined in the 1990s after Pasquale Galasso's arrest in 1992 and subsequent collaboration with justice.

The Clan Gallo-Cavalieri is a Camorra clan based in Torre Annunziata, Italy, founded in the mid-1970s by Enrico Gallo and Pasquale Gallo. It is considered one of the richest, most powerful, and most violent Camorra clans. The clan was historically opposed to the Gionta clan, leading to a bloody feud. After Enrico Gallo's death in 1985, Pasquale Gallo led the clan in a war against Valentino Gionta, which ended through the intervention of Salvatore Riina.

country_links.evidence_quote: A metà degli anni ‘90 i Cavalieri spostarono i loro affari in Spagna e Paesi Bassi gestendo il traffico della marijuana, cocaina ed eroina...

nodes.description: The Clan Gionta is a Camorra criminal organization based in Torre Annunziata, Italy. It emerged in the early 1980s under boss Valentino Gionta, engaging in cigarette smuggling, heroin trafficking, and control of the fish market. The clan was known for its violent conflicts with other Camorra groups and was heavily targeted by law enforcement, leading to the arrest of Valentino Gionta in 1985. Despite setbacks, the clan remains active with leadership passing to various members.

nodes.description: The Clan Giuliano is a Camorra organization based in central Naples, founded by Pio Vittorio Giuliano in the 1950s. It was one of the most powerful criminal groups in Campania from the 1970s to the 1990s, involved in cigarette smuggling, drug trafficking, and counterfeiting. The clan operated in neighborhoods such as Forcella, San Gaetano, Maddalena, Piazza Garibaldi, and Piazza Mercato. Several family members became pentiti (collaborators with justice), leading to its decline.

The Clan Graziano is a Camorra clan originating from Quindici, Italy. It has been involved in a long-standing conflict with the rival Clan Cava since the 1980s, initially over post-earthquake reconstruction funds. The clan was part of the larger 'Clan dei Quindiciari' before splitting. It is known for the 2002 'Strage delle donne' massacre of three women from the Cava family.

Camorra clan based in Pianura, a western suburb of Naples, Italy. Active primarily in the cement cycle, illegal building, extortion rackets, drug trafficking, and murders. Founded by Pietro Lago, who was arrested in 2004 and died in prison in 2014. The clan is now largely dismantled following arrests of key members.

nodes.description: The Clan Licciardi is a powerful Camorra syndicate based in the Secondigliano district of Naples, Italy. Founded in the mid-1980s by Gennaro Licciardi, it transformed the area into a strategic hub for drug storage and trafficking. After Gennaro's death, leadership passed to his siblings, notably Maria Licciardi. The clan is part of the Alleanza di Secondigliano cartel and has been involved in internal conflicts and large-scale drug trafficking.

country_links.evidence_quote: il clan Licciardi è attivo nei Paesi Bassi nel settore della contraffazione di marchi, dall'abbigliamento agli utensili.
country_links.context: The clan is active in the Netherlands in the counterfeit goods sector.

nodes.description: Italian Camorra organization operating in Pignataro Maggiore, Caserta province. Founded in 1965 by Vincenzo Lubrano, it maintained close ties with the Nuvoletta clan and Cosa Nostra, including Totò Riina. The Ligato faction became dominant after the decline of the original Lubrano leadership. As of recent investigations, only the Ligato faction remains active.

The Clan Magliulo was a Camorra syndicate based in Afragola, Italy, operating also in lower Lazio and Caserta. It was considered one of the most powerful Camorra families. Founded by Mario Magliulo, brother-in-law of Casalesi boss Antonio Bardellino, the clan was involved in construction contracts, control of shopping centers, drug trafficking, and a bloody feud with the Moccia clan. It suffered major asset seizures in 1990.

Italian Camorra criminal organization originating from the Quartieri Spagnoli in Naples. Founded in the 1980s by brothers Salvatore, Ciro, and Marco Mariano, former followers of the Giuliano brothers. It fought wars with the Faiano clan and the Secondigliano Alliance for control of the Quartieri Spagnoli.

The Clan Matrone is a Camorra criminal organization based in Scafati, Salerno, Italy. Founded in the 1970s, it aligned with the Nuova Famiglia against Raffaele Cutolo's Nuova Camorra Organizzata. The clan exerted near-total territorial control, often substituting for the state, and was involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and violent enforcement. Following the 2012 arrest of boss Francesco Matrone, the group became largely disarticulated, though a faction led by Giuseppe Buonocore attempted to revive its dominance until being dismantled in 2018.

The Clan Mazzarella is a Camorra criminal organization operating in several neighborhoods of Naples, Italy. Historically considered one of the most powerful Camorra clans, it was founded by the Zaza family in the 1940s and later came under the control of the Mazzarella brothers. Currently, it is divided into several branches, each with its own regent.

country_links.context: Ciro Mazzarella was arrested in Santo Domingo, indicating the clan's presence in the Dominican Republic.

nodes.description: Italian criminal organization based in Bari, founded by a confederation of the Mercante and Diomede families. Active in drug trafficking and other illicit activities in several Bari neighborhoods. Known for the 'Strage di San Valentino' in 2000, a failed attack on a rival clan. The organization has been involved in violent turf wars.

Camorra clan operating in the Rione Sanità district of Naples, Italy. Founded in the 1980s by Giuseppe Misso, known as 'o nasone. Specialized in bank robberies, postal office heists, and armored truck thefts, as well as usury, counterfeiting, and gold trafficking. Engaged in violent feuds with rival clans, including a split led by Salvatore Torino in 2005.

The Clan Moccia is the oldest and most powerful Camorra organization operating in the lower Liburia area, particularly in the municipalities of Afragola, Casoria, Arzano, Caivano and nearby, north and northeast of Naples. Founded by Gennaro Moccia in the 1960s, it was later led by his wife Anna Mazza, the first woman in Italy to face criminal proceedings for mafia crimes. The clan has a strong presence also in the Lazio region and is structured as a confederation of local criminal groups with a pyramidal hierarchy.

Italian mafia clan based in Marano di Napoli, founded in the 1960s by the Nuvoletta brothers Angelo, Lorenzo, and Ciro. It was one of the most powerful clans between the 1970s and 1990s, involved in cigarette smuggling and heroin trafficking, with strong ties to Sicilian Cosa Nostra. After the deaths of its historical leaders in the 1990s-2000s, it was replaced by the Polverino and Orlando clans.

The Clan Pariante is a Camorra criminal organization operating in the western suburbs of Naples, specifically in the municipalities of Bacoli and Monte di Procida. Founded by Rosario Pariante, it was originally part of the Di Lauro clan before splitting in 2004, triggering the First Scampia feud. The clan is involved in drug trafficking and extortion. As of 2017, the regent is Genny Pariante, son of Rosario.

Italian criminal organization based in the Japigia district of Bari, founded in the 1980s by Savino Parisi. It controls drug trafficking, extortion, and infiltrates legitimate businesses and local politics. Currently allied with the Palermiti clan, forming a 'war society' against rival factions. Despite Parisi's imprisonment, the group remains active under Eugenio Palermiti's leadership.

The Pecoraro-Renna clan is a Camorra clan originating from Battipaglia, Italy. Founded by Giovanni Pecoraro after his release from prison, it fought against the Cutolo and De Feo clans in the Sele Plain. After Giovanni's murder in 1988, his brothers Alfonso and Francesco took over, leading a bloody feud. The clan is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, usury, prostitution, and tax evasion, with operations in the Sele Plain and surrounding areas.

nodes.description: Camorra clan operating in the Quartieri Spagnoli neighborhood of Naples, Italy. Founded by Domenico Russo, known as 'Mimì dei cani', and later led by his sons. Engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and a violent feud with the Di Biasi clan. The clan emerged victorious and continues to exert control over the area.

The Clan Russo di Nola is a Camorra organization operating in Nola, Italy, founded by brothers Pasquale and Salvatore Russo in the 1980s. Originally lieutenants of Carmine Alfieri, they replaced the Alfieri clan after his downfall. Despite arrests of its leaders, the clan remains active and has expanded into new territories, forming alliances with other Camorra clans.

The Clan Sacco-Bocchetti is a Camorra organization active in the northeastern suburbs of Naples, specifically in the San Pietro a Patierno and Secondigliano districts. It was named after Gennaro Sacco and Gaetano Bocchetti, the latter being a proponent of the Secondigliano Alliance. Gennaro Sacco was killed in a Camorra attack in 2009, and Mario Bocchetti was arrested in 2017. The clan is involved in drug trafficking and extortion.

Camorra clan based in Naples, Italy, formed in the early 1980s by the Sarno brothers (Ciro, Vincenzo, Luciano, Giuseppe, Pasquale). It emerged after the dissolution of the Nuova Famiglia and engaged in conflicts with the Alleanza di Secondigliano and the De Luca Bossa clan. The clan later allied with the Mazzarella and Misso families to form a dominant cartel in Naples.

The Clan Serino is a Camorra organization originating from Sarno, Salerno, Italy. Founded by Aniello Serino, known as 'O' Pope', it was influential for over twenty years and affiliated with the Nuova Famiglia. The clan engaged in extortion, usury, drug trafficking, and video poker businesses, and infiltrated local government. As of 2019, it remains active but weakened.

Camorra clan based in Trecase, Boscoreale and Boscotrecase, controlling arms and drug trafficking in the Vesuvian area and abroad. Originating from a split from the Gionta clan in the late 1970s-early 1980s, it is considered one of the richest, most powerful and ferocious Camorra clans. Its regent, Giuseppe Gallo, is a major international cocaine broker with direct contacts with South American cartels.

English criminal organization based in Clerkenwell, London, founded in the 1980s by Terry Adams and his brothers Tommy and Patrick. Allegedly one of the most powerful in the UK, involved in drug trafficking, extortion, gold bullion hijacking, and security fraud. Linked to 25 gangland murders and connections with South American drug cartels. Influence reportedly decreased from 2000 onwards.

nodes.description: The Colacurcio Organization was a criminal group based in Seattle, Washington, founded in the 1950s by Frank Colacurcio. It operated strip clubs and vending machines as fronts for racketeering, prostitution, and money laundering. The organization was dismantled after a series of indictments in 2009-2010, culminating in Colacurcio Sr.'s death in 2010 and his son's conviction.

Mexican drug trafficking and methamphetamine producing cartel founded in 1988 by José de Jesús Amezcua Contreras and his brothers. Based in Guadalajara, Jalisco, it controlled the methamphetamine trade by obtaining ephedrine from Thailand and India. The cartel was dismantled after the arrests of its leaders in 1997-1998 and later became a branch of the Sinaloa Cartel.

Led by Theodore 'Handsome Jack' Klutas, the group consisted of ten members. They targeted mobsters because they were unlikely to go to police and could pay ransoms.

The Colombo crime family is an Italian American Mafia crime family and one of the Five Families of New York City. Founded in 1928 by Joe Profaci, it is the youngest of the Five Families and has a history of instability and infighting, including three internal wars. The family engages in racketeering, gambling, loansharking, extortion, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. It remains active, though weakened by leadership turnover and prosecutions.

Originated as a bootlegging organization under the Carlino brothers in the 1920s, later taken over by Giuseppe Roma and evolved into the Denver branch of La Cosa Nostra. Engaged in extortion, loan sharking, drug trafficking, and other rackets. Believed defunct by the 2000s after the death of Clarence Smaldone.

Criminal organization and street gang based in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1988. Involved in murder, drug trafficking, and violence, with one of the largest drug operations in New England. Known for wearing Philadelphia Phillies or Pittsburgh Pirates hats and driving expensive vehicles. In 2015, 48 members were arrested in a major gang takedown.

The Comanchero Motorcycle Club is an outlaw motorcycle gang based in Australia, with chapters in Southeast Asia and New Zealand. Founded in 1968 by William George 'Jock' Ross in Sydney, the club is known for its violent history, including the 1984 Milperra massacre. The Comancheros are involved in drug trafficking and have been engaged in ongoing conflicts with rival clubs such as the Hells Angels and Bandidos.

nodes.description: Brazilian criminal faction originating in Altamira, Pará, founded around 2018. It emerged from prison disputes, breaking from Comando Vermelho and allying with PCC. Active in drug trafficking, homicides, and prison control, with operations in Pará and Amazonian drug routes. Maintains ties with Colombian cartels and former FARC members.

One of the two largest criminal organizations in Brazil, founded in 1979 at the Cândido Mendes prison on Ilha Grande, Rio de Janeiro. It originated from the Falange Vermelha and was created by Rogério Lemgruber. nodes.description: The Cordì 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Locri, Calabria, Italy, founded in the 1950s. It is involved in racketeering, murder, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. The clan has been engaged in a long-running blood feud with the Cataldo 'ndrina. Despite arrests of key members, the clan remains active.

The Corleone Mafia family is a Cosa Nostra crime family based in Corleone, Sicily, founded around the 1900s by Angelo Gagliano. It rose to become the most powerful mafia family in Italy and the world under Totò Riina, winning the Second Mafia War in the 1980s. After a period of repression in the early 1990s, many members were imprisoned, but the family remains active with about 70 members.

The Corleonesi was an alliance of Mafia families within the Sicilian Mafia, formed in the 1970s. Led by Luciano Leggio, Salvatore Riina, Bernardo Provenzano, and others, it took over the Sicilian Mafia Commission and imposed a dictatorship over Cosa Nostra. The coalition waged the Second Mafia War from 1978–1983 and dominated until 2006.

The Cornbread Mafia was a group of Kentucky men who operated the largest domestic marijuana production operation in U.S. history, based in central Kentucky. Founded in the late 1970s by Joe Keith Bickett and others, the group grew marijuana across 30 farms in 10 states. The term was first publicly used by federal prosecutors in 1989 after a massive bust. The group was known for its code of silence, which prevented a Continuing Criminal Enterprise prosecution.

The Corsican mafia is a collective of criminal groups originating from Corsica, tied to both the French underworld and Italian organized crime. It operates in France, North Africa, and Latin America, engaging in activities such as drug trafficking, racketeering, and gambling. The group was involved in the French Connection heroin trafficking operation in the mid-20th century. Today, it consists of multiple families and gangs, including the Brise de Mer successors and the Petit Bar Gang.

nodes.description: The Cortesi brothers were four Italian-descended siblings who operated as gangsters in London in the early 20th century. They engaged in protection racketeering of gamblers and bookmakers, and were rivals of the Sabini family. The brothers were involved in a violent confrontation at the Fratellanza Social Club in 1922, leading to arrests and convictions. The group was active from the 1900s until the deaths of the brothers between 1938 and 1972.

nodes.description: The Cotroni crime family was an Italian Canadian crime family based in Montreal, Quebec, established in the 1940s by Vincenzo Cotroni. It was considered a branch of the Bonanno crime family of New York City. The family controlled territory in southern Quebec and Ontario, engaging in racketeering, drug trafficking, and other illegal activities. An internal war in the late 1970s led to the rise of the Sicilian Rizzuto faction, and the family became defunct by the 2000s.

nodes.description: The County Road Cutters are a hooligan firm associated with Premier League football club Everton F.C. The Cowboy Mafia was a nickname for a group of marijuana smugglers operating in the United States during the 1970s. Based in Texas, they imported over 106 tons of marijuana from Colombia using shrimp boats. The group was arrested in 1978 and 26 members were convicted in 1979. Known primarily for fuel theft (huachicoleo) and drug trafficking, it has been in violent conflict with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. Despite leadership arrests, the group remains active.

nodes.description: Mexican criminal organization dedicated to drug trafficking, based in Tepalcatepec, Michoacán. Founded in 2018 by Juan José Farías Álvarez alias 'El Abuelo'. Known for violent confrontations with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) and for using tactics such as explosive-laden drones and roadblocks. Currently operates under the protection of Carteles Unidos.

Mexican criminal group founded in 2012 by Felipe de Jesús Pérez Luna, alias El Ojos, operating primarily in Tláhuac, Iztapalapa, Milpa Alta, Xochimilco, and the State of Mexico. It emerged from splinter groups of the Beltrán Leyva Cartel and engages in drug trafficking, homicide, extortion, kidnapping, vehicle theft, fuel theft, and human trafficking. The group is currently led by relatives of El Ojos and remains active.

Mexican criminal organization based in Michoacán, founded in the 1970s by Emilio Valencia Barragán. Dedicated to drug trafficking, particularly cocaine, to Mexico and the United States. Known for using avocado production as a front. Became one of the most violent and powerful cartels in Mexico, responsible for a third of US cocaine consumption. Disarticulated by 2009.

nodes.description: Mexican criminal and terrorist organization formed in 2015 after a split from Los Zetas following the capture of Omar Treviño Morales. Based in Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas, it engages in drug trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, human trafficking, money laundering, and murder. Designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the U.S. State Department in February 2025. Controls territory in several Mexican states and has operational presence in the United States, Guatemala, Honduras, and Colombia.

Originally formed as Gente Nueva, the armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel, it became independent in 2023 after internal disputes with Los Chapitos. Based in Sonora, it operates in Chihuahua, Sonora, and Sinaloa, and is currently active.

nodes.description: Mexican criminal organization originating in Jalisco, formed in 2017 as a split from the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG). Led by Enrique Sánchez Martínez 'El Cholo', Emiliano Santiago Sánchez 'El M menor Mogli', and Érick Valencia Salazar 'El 85'. It operates in the Guadalajara metropolitan area and is financed by the Sinaloa Cartel. The group is engaged in a violent territorial dispute with CJNG.

Mexican criminal organization formed in 2010 to expel Los Zetas from Michoacán and Jalisco. Composed of members from various cartels including Tepalcatepec, Los Viagras, Sinaloa, La Familia Michoacana, Gulf, and Knights Templar. Known for drug trafficking in the Tierra Caliente region and ongoing conflict with CJNG. Designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the U.S. State Department in February 2025.

nodes.description: One of the earliest crime families in New York City, based in Manhattan's Little Italy. Founded by Salvatore D'Aquila in the 1910s after breaking off from the Morello family and absorbing remnants of the Brooklyn Camorra. Active in racketeering, extortion, and murder until D'Aquila's murder in 1928, after which the family was taken over by Manfredi Mineo and eventually became part of the modern Gambino crime family.

American criminal street gang based in Algiers, New Orleans, Louisiana, formed by teenagers from the DeGaulle Manor Public Housing Complex and Fischer Projects. Active from 2004 to 2017, involved in drug trafficking, multiple murders, and violent crimes. The gang was tracked by NOPD since the mid-2000s and listed as a threat by the FBI in 2011.

nodes.description: The D.C. Blacks is an African-American prison gang in the United States whose members are from Washington D.C. They are allied with the Black Guerrilla Family and rival the Aryan Brotherhood. Formed due to the concentration of D.C. inmates in federal facilities, they are one of the largest prison gangs within penitentiaries but smaller than gangs like the Bloods and Crips.

nodes.description: The Dallas crime family, also known as the Civello crime family, was an Italian-American Mafia crime family based in Dallas, Texas. Founded around 1910 by Carlo Piranio, it operated primarily in the Dallas metropolitan area and throughout Texas, Oklahoma, and Arkansas. The family was involved in racketeering, loansharking, drug trafficking, and other criminal activities. It became defunct in the 1990s.

DarkMarket was an English-language cybercrime forum created by Renukanth Subramaniam in London. It facilitated the buying and selling of stolen identities and credit card data, with 2,500 users at its peak. The forum was infiltrated by FBI agent J. Keith Mularski, leading to over 60 arrests worldwide. It was shut down in 2008, and Subramaniam was sentenced to nearly five years in prison in 2010.

country_links.evidence_quote: German prosecutors in the cities of Koblenz and Oldenburg said 12 January 2021 that they had shut down what was 'probably the largest illegal marketplace on the Darknet ' called DarkMarket and physically arrested the man believed to operate it near Germany's border with Denmark.
country_links.context: The DarkMarket darknet market was shut down by German prosecutors, who arrested its operator near Germany's border with Denmark.

country_links.evidence_quote: Working with our international partners in the United Kingdom, Germany, and Turkey, the FBI conducted a two-year undercover operation to penetrate the organization and bring it to its knees.
country_links.context: The FBI worked with Turkey as an international partner in the operation against DarkMarket.

nodes.description: The Daybreak Boys was a New York City street gang formed in the late 1840s. Active along the waterfront, they were known for unprovoked murder, sabotage, and theft. By 1852, they were suspected of 20 to 40 murders and stealing $200,000 in goods. The gang was broken up by police in 1859 after several gunfights.

The De Luca Bossa clan is a Neapolitan Camorra clan operating in the eastern suburbs of Naples, particularly Ponticelli and Cercola. Founded by Antonio De Luca Bossa in the 1990s, it emerged from a split with the Sarno clan and engaged in a bloody war for territorial control. The clan is involved in racketeering, extortion, drug trafficking, and murder. Despite leadership arrests, it remains active.

country_links.evidence_quote: Pasquale Brunese, a drug trafficker working for the clan was arrested in Valencia , Spain , in 2015, after seven years hiding from the Italian police.
country_links.context: A drug trafficker working for the clan was arrested in Valencia, Spain, after hiding there for seven years.

nodes.description: The De Stefano 'ndrina is a powerful clan of the 'Ndrangheta criminal organization based in Reggio Calabria, Italy. It rose to prominence in the 1970s after the first 'Ndrangheta war, taking control of construction and drug trafficking. The clan has strong ramifications throughout Italy, particularly in Lombardy, Tuscany, Emilia-Romagna, and Liguria. Several members have been listed among Italy's most wanted fugitives.

Dead Man Incorporated (DMI) is a predominantly white organized crime enterprise founded in the late 1990s in the Maryland Department of Corrections by Perry Roark, James Sweeney, and Brian Jordan. Initially allied with the Black Guerrilla Family, the gang expanded into drug trafficking, murder, and other crimes. It operates in prisons and streets across Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia, with an estimated 370 members. Internal divisions have emerged over ideology and direction.

Irish American criminal street gang active in Lower Manhattan from the 1830s to 1860s. They were founded by disgruntled members of the Roach Guards and were known for their rivalry with the Bowery Boys. The gang engaged in street fighting, assault, murder, and rioting, and supported Tammany Hall politicians. Their symbol was a dead rabbit on a pike.

nodes.description: The DeCavalcante crime family is an Italian-American Mafia crime family operating primarily in North Jersey, particularly in Elizabeth, Newark, Linden, and West New York. Founded around the 1900s by Phil Amari, it is considered by some to be the 'Sixth Family' due to its strong ties with New York's Five Families. The family engages in racketeering, gambling, drug trafficking, extortion, and other illicit activities. It maintains alliances with several other Mafia families, including the Gambino and Philadelphia families.

country_links.evidence_quote: The family also has links to Ribera in Sicily , where many of the organization's members have their origins.

nodes.description: The Decepticons were a Brooklyn street gang active from the mid-1980s into the early 1990s. Named after the antagonists of the Transformers franchise, they were known for flash-mob style attacks and muggings. The gang originated in Brooklyn and expanded across New York City, with offshoots in Queens and the Bronx. Some former members later became notable in hip-hop music.

nodes.description: The Detroit Partnership is an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Detroit, Michigan, founded around 1908 by Pietro Mirabile. It operates primarily in the Greater Detroit area, with additional territory in Ohio, Ontario, and Las Vegas. The family has been involved in racketeering, gambling, loan-sharking, labor racketeering, narcotics trafficking, and other illegal activities. Despite RICO prosecutions in the 1990s, the organization remains active in the 21st century.

nodes.description: The Di Lauro clan is an Italian crime clan and part of the Camorra in Naples, founded in 1982 by Paolo Di Lauro. It operates in several neighborhoods of Naples and surrounding municipalities. At its peak in the late 1990s and early 2000s, the clan earned over €500,000 daily from drug sales, making Secondigliano the largest open-air drug market in Europe. Despite arrests, the clan has adapted with a business-oriented model, focusing on international smuggling and counterfeiting.

nodes.description: A gang of thieves active in the late 1960s and 1970s, known for burglarizing wealthy Americans' homes while the victims were at dinner. Based in the United States, the gang was led by brothers-in-law Peter Salerno and Dominick Latella. They stole millions in jewels, targeting families like the DuPonts and Flaglers. The gang avoided violence and carried no weapons.

The Dirty Dozen Motorcycle Club was an outlaw motorcycle club based in Arizona, founded in 1964 by twelve founding members. It became the largest and most violent motorcycle gang in the state, involved in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, prostitution, assault, and murder. The club merged with the Hells Angels in 1997.

nodes.description: The Dixie Mafia is a loosely connected criminal organization originally based in Biloxi, Mississippi, operating primarily in the Southern United States from the 1960s onward. It engaged in burglary, theft, robbery, drug trafficking, contract killings, and blackmail. Unlike the American Mafia, members were not connected by family or ethnicity but by a common goal of profit. The group is now a general term for independent White Southern criminal networks.

Street gang based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, founded in 2006. Involved in drug and weapons trafficking, operating from a highrise complex on Dixon Road. Dismantled in 2013 after Project Traveller, with 43 members arrested. Still considered active.

Assyrian criminal organization active in southwestern Sydney, Australia, originating from the Assyrian Kings gang. Involved in drug trafficking, murders, and public shootings. Resurrected in the early 2000s under the name DLASTHR after the original gang dissolved following the murder of off-duty police officer David Carty in 1997.

country_links.evidence_quote: In October 2006, Raphael Joseph was arrested in San Diego United States .
country_links.context: Raphael Joseph, a member of DLASTHR, was arrested in San Diego, United States, and later extradited to Australia.

nodes.description: A group of Ukrainian oligarchs, politicians, and organized crime figures, and formerly Soviet politicians, based in Dnipro (formerly Dnipropetrovsk). It emerged after the Great Purge and was firmly established in the 1950s-1960s under Leonid Brezhnev. The group wielded powerful influence in Ukraine and was involved in black market activities. It declined after Brezhnev's death and Gorbachev's rise.

Primarily Afro-Caribbean street gang based in Moss Side, Manchester, United Kingdom. Originated from the Pepperhill Crew in the 1980s and named after Dodington Close. Engaged in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, robbery, kidnapping, and murder. Known for rivalries with the Cheetham Hill Gang and Gooch Close Gang, contributing to the 'Gunchester' era. Still active as of the 2000s.

A Palestinian clan from the Gaza Strip known for its long-running rivalry with Hamas. Involved in extortion, smuggling, arms dealing, and killings. Members have been affiliated with Fatah, Hamas, Popular Resistance Committees, and Al-Qaeda. The clan was behind the 2007 kidnapping of British journalist Alan Johnston.

nodes.description: The Dojin-kai is a yakuza organization headquartered in Kurume, Fukuoka, Japan, founded in 1971 by Isoji Koga. It is a designated yakuza syndicate with approximately 310 members, known for its militant nature and large-scale drug trafficking, particularly methamphetamine. The group has been involved in violent conflicts with other yakuza groups, including the Yamaguchi-gumi and its own splinter group, Kyushu Seido-kai.

nodes.description: Dominicans Don't Play (DDP) is a Dominican-American street gang formed in Manhattan, New York, in 1991. Known for using machetes and knives, they are involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. The gang operates across New York City, New Jersey, and internationally, with ties to Colombian cartels for cocaine distribution.

country_links.evidence_quote: Spanish police in Madrid noted a growing gang presence of the DDP. Spanish police report 130 documented DDP members, making them the largest in Spain.
country_links.context: The DDP has a documented presence in Spain, with 130 members reported by Spanish police, making it the largest and most violent street gang in Spain.

nodes.description: The Downtown Gang was a criminal organization based in Galveston, Texas, founded around 1920 by Johnny Jack Nounes. It dominated organized crime in Galveston during Prohibition, engaging in bootlegging, gambling, and other illegal activities. The gang had connections with the Chicago Outfit and New York mobsters. It declined after 1935.

nodes.description: The Dutch Mob was a New York pickpocket gang active during the late nineteenth century. Formed in the late 1860s by Little Freddie, Mike Kurtz, and Johnny Irving, it grew to around 300 members. The gang operated in Manhattan's Bowery area, using staged street fights to pickpocket crowds. Police crackdowns in 1877 led to its dissolution.

nodes.description: The East Harlem Purple Gang was an Italian-American organized crime group based in New York City, active from the early 1970s to the 1980s. It consisted of hit-men and heroin dealers who were semi-independent from the Italian-American Mafia but allied with several crime families, particularly the Genovese family. The gang dominated heroin distribution in East Harlem, Italian Harlem, and the Bronx. At its peak, it had about 30 members and 80 associates, and was considered an unofficial sixth family.

nodes.description: The Eastman Gang was a predominantly Jewish-American street gang that dominated parts of the New York City underworld from the late 1890s to the early 1910s. Founded by Monk Eastman, the gang operated in Manhattan's Lower East Side, engaging in armed robbery, theft, illegal gambling, extortion, prostitution, and opium peddling. It succeeded the Whyos as a prominent non-Irish gang and had strong political connections through Tammany Hall. The gang dissolved in the early 1910s.

Based in the Elephant and Castle area, they raided West End stores and sometimes posed as housemaids to rob homes. Anti-fascist, anti-racist, and anti-drug hardcore crew founded in the late 1980s by Elgin James in Boston, Massachusetts. Originally fought Neo-Nazis and racist groups in the punk scene, but later accused of unprovoked violence and intimidation. Classified by the FBI as a street gang.

Primarily African American, it engages in drug trafficking, weapons smuggling, and murder. The gang is in direct opposition to the Central Park Gang and has been involved in ongoing violent conflicts.

The Fruit Town Piru is a set of the Piru gang alliance, part of the larger Bloods alliance, formed in the 1970s in Compton, California. Named after fruit-named streets in their neighborhood, the gang is primarily African-American and known for its rivalry with the Mob Piru Bloods. It has been involved in violent feuds and has affiliations with rappers such as Chris Brown and Soulja Boy.

Swedish criminal network founded by Daniel Maiorana in the late 1990s, originally named Tumba Lords. Based in Tumba, Stockholm, the group engages in car thefts, motorcycle thefts, armed robberies, and drug trafficking. Membership is estimated at around 40 individuals, with a core of 12 men.

Mexican criminal organization originating from the Tepito neighborhood of Mexico City, founded around 2016. It emerged either as a self-defense group against the Unión Tepito or as a splinter faction led by Roberto Moyado. Engages in extortion, kidnapping, drug trafficking, and murder. Despite arrests of key leaders, the group remains active.

Fujianese organized crime refers to crime syndicates composed of Fujianese people, similar to triad gangs. The term primarily covers Fujianese immigrant gangs in Hong Kong, but also includes native crime syndicates in Fujian province. They have been involved in attacks against Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters and collaborate with international criminal groups such as the Yakuza and American Mafia.

A Korean-American street gang based in Fullerton, California, founded in 1996. Members were originally from other gangs such as LVM, SZA, and Wah Ching. The gang emerged as a collective identity after other gangs disbanded in Fullerton.

nodes.description: The Galloway Boys are a gang based in Southern Ontario, Canada, originating in the Scarborough district of Toronto. Founded in the early 1980s, they expanded into Durham Region and Kawartha Lakes. They are involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, murder, burglary, and racketeering, and have been linked to multiple gang-related violence incidents including the Danzig Street shooting.

The Gambino family is one of the Five Families of New York and one of the most powerful in the United States. Originating from the Black Hand gang led by Ignazio Lupo and Giuseppe Morello in East Harlem, it evolved under Salvatore D'Aquila and later Al Mineo. The family was formally established as one of the Five Families by Salvatore Maranzano after the Castellammarese War. It remains active in organized crime activities such as gambling and racketeering.

nodes.description: The Gang des Tractions Avant was a criminal gang in the Pigalle quarter of Paris, composed of former Carlingue militia members, lapsed police officers, and criminals from the French Resistance. Active in the mid-20th century, the gang was named after its preferred vehicle, the Citroën 11CV 'Traction'. Its methods influenced later gangs and inspired various cultural works.

The Gangster Disciples are an African-American street and prison gang founded in Chicago in 1966 by Larry Hoover and David Barksdale. Originally formed as the Black Gangster Disciple Nation, the group split in 1989 into the Gangster Disciple Nation and the Black Disciple Nation. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, assault, firearms violations, fraud, homicide, money laundering, and organized crime, with an estimated 30,000 members in Chicago and operations across the United States and internationally.

nodes.description: The Garduña is a mythical secret criminal society said to have been founded in Spain in the late Middle Ages, around 1417, with statutes approved in Toledo in 1420. It was allegedly involved in robbery, kidnapping, arson, and murder-for-hire. However, historians consider it a fictional organization, with all references traced back to a 19th-century book. It is often cited as a foundational myth for Italian mafias like the Camorra, Mafia, and 'Ndrangheta.

British street gang based in Brixton, South London, formed in the late 2000s. Known for drug trafficking, murder, theft, and money laundering. Considered one of the most dangerous gangs in South London by 2012, responsible for multiple murders and violent incidents. Membership declined in the early 2010s due to incarceration of leaders.

The Gas House Gang was a New York City street gang founded in the 1890s, based in the Gas House district of Manhattan. They controlled the area along Third Avenue from 11th to 18th Street, specializing in armed robbery, extortion, and operating brothels. The gang committed an estimated 30 to 40 robberies per night and dominated the district for over two decades until being absorbed by the Five Points Gang in 1910.

Canadian outlaw motorcycle club founded in 2013 in Musquodoboit Harbour, Nova Scotia. Operates as a support club for the Hells Angels in Canada, with chapters in Ontario and formerly Nova Scotia. Known for rapid expansion and rivalry with Bacchus Motorcycle Club.

Founded by Charles 'Lucky' Luciano in the 1930s, it is the oldest and largest of the Five Families. Known for its secrecy and white-collar rackets, it has been considered the most powerful Mafia family in the United States. The family is currently led by Liborio 'Barney' Bellomo.

The faction has maintained a strong presence in Northern Jersey since the early Prohibition era. Notable members include Guarino 'Willie' Moretti, Gerardo 'Jerry' Catena, and Louis 'Bobby' Manna.

nodes.description: Gente Nueva is a large group of well-trained gunmen serving as an elite armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel. Founded in 1995 in Sonora, Mexico, it was created to counter the Juárez Cartel's influence in northwestern Mexico. The group has been involved in drug trafficking, kidnapping, and murder, and has engaged in a prolonged turf war with the Juárez Cartel and its enforcer wing, La Línea. As of 2012, Gente Nueva and the Sinaloa Cartel had emerged victorious in the conflict.

nodes.description: George Street is a Bloods-affiliated street gang based in Belize City, Belize, allegedly formed in the late 1980s by US deportee Heathcliff Reyes. It is one of the country's earliest gangs and has been involved in violent conflicts with rival gangs. The gang's territory was estimated as among the largest in Belize in 2018, with membership ranging from 40 to 150. As of 2021, it remains one of the largest gangs in Belize.

The Georgian mafia is an organized crime network originating in Georgia, known for producing the largest number of 'thieves in law' in post-Soviet states. It controls and regulates many Russian-speaking mafia groups and is active in Russia and Europe. The organization has two major clans from Tbilisi and Kutaisi, with the Kutaisi Clan being particularly well represented. Its criminal activities include arms trafficking, extortion, money laundering, and murder.

It was part of the Hongmen overseas network and provided mutual aid for Chinese migrants, aiming to overthrow the Qing dynasty. The society was involved in violent conflicts with rival secret societies and was suppressed by colonial authorities from the 1890s.

nodes.description: The Ghetto Boys is a street gang based in New Cross, Lewisham and Deptford, South London. Formed in the 1970s on the Woodpecker Estate, it is primarily composed of Black British members. The gang has been involved in drug trafficking, murder, assault, and robbery, and had a notable conflict with the Peckham Boys. By the mid-late 2000s, the gang declined and splintered, with offshoots like Shower and 814 emerging.

The Ghetto Brothers were a gang and music group founded in New York City's South Bronx in the late 1960s. They were involved in politics, particularly the Puerto Rican independence movement, and aimed to uplift young Latino and Black men. The gang spread to much of the Northeastern United States and later merged with the Savage Nomads to form Los Solidos in Connecticut.

nodes.description: The Ghost Shadows was a Chinese American street gang prominent in New York City's Chinatown from the early 1970s to the mid 1990s. Formed in 1971 by immigrants from Taiwan and Hong Kong, it was affiliated with the On Leong Tong. The gang engaged in extortion, kidnapping, murder, racketeering, drug trafficking, and illegal gambling. It became defunct due to federal RICO crackdowns in the 1990s.

nodes.description: The Giuliano clan is a powerful Neapolitan Camorra clan originating in the Forcella district of Naples. Founded by Pio Vittorio Giuliano in the early 1950s, it initially focused on cigarette smuggling. Under Luigi Giuliano, it became the most powerful Camorra group in Naples from the 1970s to the mid-1980s. The clan was a key member of the Nuova Famiglia alliance that defeated the Nuova Camorra Organizzata. As of 2025, only a small faction remains active.

nodes.description: The Goda-ikka is a yakuza group based in Yamaguchi, Japan, formed in 1948 as the Goda-gumi by Koichi Goda. It is the largest yakuza group in Yamaguchi Prefecture, with an estimated 30 members. The group was renamed Goda-ikka in 1968 and became a designated yakuza group in 1992. It is a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai.

Organised crime group based in Moss Side, South Manchester, England, founded in the late 1980s. Primarily involved in drug trafficking, weapon trafficking, robbery, and murder. Known for violent disputes with rival gangs such as the Doddington Gang and Moss Side Bloods. Still active as of the present.

The Gopher Gang was an early 20th-century New York street gang based in Hell's Kitchen, Manhattan. Formed in the 1890s from various local street gangs, it numbered around 500 members and controlled territory from Fourth to Forty-Second Street and Seventh to Eleventh Avenue. The gang engaged in burglary, armed robbery, assault, prostitution, and illegal gambling. It declined in the 1910s.

The Goto-gumi was a Japanese yakuza organization founded by Tadamasa Goto. Originally based in Fujinomiya, Shizuoka Prefecture, it moved to Tokyo in 1991 and became an affiliate of the Yamaguchi-gumi. The gang was involved in financial, real estate, construction, entertainment, and political activities, and was notorious for the assault on filmmaker Juzo Itami. It was dissolved in 2008 after Goto's expulsion from the Yamaguchi-gumi.

nodes.description: The Grady Gang was a New York City sneak thief gang during the 1860s, organized by fence John D. 'Traveling Mike' Grady after the American Civil War. The gang operated in Broadway's 'Thieves Exchange' and was known for the robbery of $2 million from financier Rufus L. Lord in 1866. Most members retired by the end of the decade, but Grady continued as a fence.

Gran Grif is the largest and most powerful criminal organization in the Artibonite department of Haiti, based in Savien. Founded around 2016 by former congressman Prophane Victor, it engages in murder, rape, mass abduction, forced child recruitment, and other violent abuses. The gang was responsible for 80% of reported civilian deaths in Artibonite in 2022 and perpetrated the 2024 Pont-Sondé attack that killed at least 115 people. It has been designated a terrorist organization by the Dominican Republic and the United States.

Founded in the late 19th century, the extended family played a key role in the Sicilian Cosa Nostra, with members serving as secretaries of the Sicilian Mafia Commission. nodes.description: The Hard Livings gang is a large street gang and organized crime group based in Manenberg, Cape Town, South Africa. nodes.description: The Henry Street Gang was a Chicago street gang formed by Chris Merry in the early 1890s. Based in Chicago's Southwest Side, they committed armed robbery against local merchants and street peddlers, often posing as push cart vendors. They developed a robbery method called the 'kick in' and operated for several years until Merry was hanged for murdering his wife, after which the gang dissolved.

Known for brutal attacks on passersby, they operated with impunity until 1853 when police Captain George W. Walling formed the Strong Arm Squad to suppress them. The gang was disbanded within two weeks, with members fleeing the district.

nodes.description: The Hook Gang was a street gang and river pirate group active in New York City in the 1860s and 1870s. Far-right hooligan group based around German football club Chemnitzer FC, founded in the early 1990s by Thomas Haller. The group engaged in fights with other hooligan firms and was banned from the stadium in 2006. Officially dissolved in 2007, it continues as a loose network of 20-30 members.

The Hop Sing Tong is a Chinese American tong established in 1875. It operates multiple branches across the United States, including in cities such as San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Seattle. The organization is historically associated with Chinese immigrant communities and has been involved in both legitimate and illicit activities.

The Hopi Boys are an Afro-Curaçaoan criminal group based in the south-east region of Amsterdam, Netherlands. They are one of the most influential gangs in the Dutch capital, controlling rackets, drug dealing, and prostitution. The group is predominantly Afro-Curaçaoan and has allies such as the Green gang and rivals like the Kloekhorststraat Gang.

nodes.description: The Hornec gang is a Gitanes criminal group from the Paris region, led by three brothers from Montreuil. It controls racketeering, drug dealing, and illegal slot machines in Paris, with connections to the Corsican mafia and Maghrebian gangs. The gang rose after the 1994 assassination of crime boss Claude Genova and became the most influential in Paris, but its influence declined after arrests in 2006.

Founded by Hussein al-Houthi, the group opposes the Yemeni government and is backed by Iran. nodes.description: The Hoxton Gang was an independent street gang based in Soho, London, during the interwar years. They fought against Charles 'Darby' Sabini and the 'Italian Mob' for control of gambling clubs and racetracks. In 1936, members attacked a bookmaker at Lewes racetrack, leading to convictions. The gang was led by Jimmy Spinks.

The Hudson Dusters were a New York City street gang formed in the late 1890s by Circular Jack, Kid Yorke, and Goo Goo Knox. Based in Manhattan's West Side, they controlled the Hudson River docks and engaged in burglary, armed robbery, and narcotics. The gang had ties to Tammany Hall and was known for cocaine-fueled violence. They were active until around 1917.

nodes.description: The Inagawa-kai is the third largest yakuza group in Japan, based in the Kantō region. Founded in 1949 by Kakuji Inagawa in Atami, Shizuoka, it initially focused on illegal gambling and later expanded into drug trafficking, extortion, and prostitution. It was one of the first yakuza organizations to operate overseas and has an estimated 1,600 members.

The Independent Cartel of Acapulco was a Mexican criminal gang based in Acapulco, Guerrero, formed in 2010 as a split from the Beltrán-Leyva Cartel after the death of Arturo Beltrán Leyva. It engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and murder, known for flaying victims' faces. The group was severely damaged by 2011 and faded from public view, with its territory taken over by rival La Barredora.

nodes.description: The Kozakura-ikka is a yakuza organization based in Kagoshima, Kyushu, Japan, with an estimated 40 active members. It was formed in 1948 by Seizo Osato. The group is noted for its unique policy, the 'Kozakura Monroe Doctrine', of not operating outside Kagoshima Prefecture and not allowing other yakuza syndicates to enter. Its criminal activities include protection racketeering, drug trafficking, and unlawful involvement in public works.

nodes.description: The Kudo-kai is a yakuza group headquartered in Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, Japan, founded before WWII as a bakuto organization named Kudo-gumi by Genji Kudo. It is the largest yakuza group in the Kitakyushu area, known for its militant stance and conflicts with the Yamaguchi-gumi. The group has been designated as a particularly nefarious organization by the National Police Agency and was registered under the Organized Crime Countermeasures Law in 1992.

Predominantly African-American prison gang formed in Folsom State Prison in the mid-1980s by inmates from the San Francisco Bay Area. The name combines the Swahili word for ten (kumi) with San Francisco's area code 415. Members often incorporate African symbols and Swahili language into their culture and tattoos. The gang operates in several California prisons and selected areas.

Kuratong Baleleng is an organized crime syndicate in the Philippines, originally established in 1986 as an anti-communist vigilante group. It became one of the largest syndicates in the country, involved in kidnapping, drug trafficking, extortion, and other crimes. The group gained nationwide attention after a 1995 shootout with police in Quezon City. Despite the death of its first leader, the syndicate has scattered across provinces and some members have entered politics.

The Kurdish mafia comprises organized crime groups run by ethnic Kurds, operating primarily in Western Asia, Europe, and North America. Their main activities include drug and arms trafficking, contract killing, and migrant smuggling. They have been accused of funneling profits to the PKK and have cooperated with other crime groups. The mafia emerged from banditry during the decline of the Ottoman Empire.

nodes.description: The Kyodo-kai is a yakuza group based in Hiroshima, Japan, formed in January 1969 by Kokichi Morita after the disbanding of its predecessor, the Takahashi-gumi. It is a designated yakuza group with an estimated 60 active members and is the second largest yakuza group in the Chugoku region. The group has been a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai since 1996.

The Kyokuryū-kai is a yakuza criminal organization based on the Okinawa island of Japan, with an estimated membership of 210–270. It was formed in 1970 as the Okinawa-rengo Kyokuryu-kai by two gangs, the Naha Clan and the Koza Clan. It was Okinawa's largest organized crime group from 1983 until 1990 when a splinter group, the Okinawa Kyokuryu-kai, broke away. The group has been in conflict with the Yamaguchi-gumi and its official policy forbids drug trafficking.

The Kyokuto-kai is a yakuza organization based in Tokyo, Japan, founded by Aiji Sekiguchi. It was registered as a designated yakuza group under the Organized Crime Countermeasures Law in July 1993. In the early 2000s, it was involved in a feud with the rival Matsuba-kai, leading to shootings. As of the article, it has about 300 members and is led by Jin Takahashi.

The Kyosei-kai is a yakuza group based in Hiroshima, Japan, formed in May 1964 by bakuto Tatsuo Yamamura from seven yakuza clans. Known for fierce conflicts with other groups, particularly the Yamaguchi-gumi, it has been a leading member of anti-Yamaguchi federations. The group has around 120 members and is led by Susumu Arase.

The Kyushu Seido-kai was a yakuza organization based in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, formed in 2006 as a splinter group from the Dojin-kai. It engaged in armed conflicts with its former parent syndicate, using automatic firearms and grenades, and was designated as a yakuza group in 2008. The group was involved in drug trafficking and loansharking, and dissolved in June 2013, later reorganizing under new names.

La Barredora is a Mexican criminal gang based in Tabasco, formed in 2008 as a split-off from the Beltrán-Leyva Cartel. It operates primarily in Acapulco and surrounding states, engaging in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, murder, kidnapping, arms trafficking, and illegal fuel extraction. The group is known for its rivalry with the Independent Cartel of Acapulco and links to the Sinaloa Cartel. Its leader, Hernán Bermúdez Requena, was captured in Paraguay in 2025.

nodes.description: La Línea is the main faction of the Juárez Cartel, originally formed as an enforcement unit composed of former police and military personnel. Based in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, it was founded in 2008 by Juan Pablo Ledezma. The group is involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and kidnappings, and has been responsible for numerous massacres in Ciudad Juárez. It has formed alliances with the CJNG and Los Chapitos to combat the Sinaloa Cartel.

Founded in 2010 by Eznel Cortés Jiménez and Óscar Osvaldo García Montoya, it operated primarily in Mexico City and the State of Mexico. The group was involved in homicide, kidnapping, extortion, and other crimes. It was dismantled by 2016.

Formed in 2011 as a splinter group after the original La Familia Michoacana lost power. Led by brothers Johnny and José Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga. Operates primarily in Michoacán, Guerrero, and the State of Mexico, and is involved in distributing cocaine, fentanyl, and methamphetamine to the United States. nodes.description: La Raza Nation is a street gang founded in Chicago in 1973, primarily composed of Hispanic members of Mexican or Central American origin. Its colors are green, white, and red, and its symbols include the Mexican flag, cross, and six-point star. The gang is affiliated with the Folk Nation and has been involved in conflicts with various other gangs. It has expanded from Chicago to other states including Illinois, Wisconsin, Ohio, Florida, and Georgia.

The La Rosa 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a criminal organization based in Calabria, Italy. Founded by Antonio La Rosa in the 1970s, the clan operates primarily in Tropea and is allied with the Mancuso 'ndrina. They have been involved in feuds with rival clans such as the Piserà 'ndrina and have been subject to multiple law enforcement operations, including asset seizures and arrests for murder, extortion, and arms trafficking.

Mexican criminal organization founded in 2009 in Tepito, Mexico City, under the tutelage of Édgar Valdez Villarreal. It engages in drug trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, murder, money laundering, and other crimes. The group operates primarily in Greater Mexico City and several Mexican states, and is known for using minors in criminal activities. It remains active as of 2021.

nodes.description: The Lanzino 'ndrina is a criminal clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Cosenza, Calabria, Italy. It is allied with the Alvaro clan. The organization has been involved in extortion, public contract rigging, and vote-buying, with operations spanning from the 1980s to the present. Key members include Ettore Lanzino, who died in prison in 2024.

Its primary objective is to merge Kashmir with Pakistan and seeks destruction of India, Hinduism, and Judaism through jihad. Designated as a terrorist group by the UN and many countries, it has carried out major attacks in India including the 2008 Mumbai attacks. It is supported by Pakistan's ISI and operates primarily in Kashmir.

nodes.description: The Latella 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a mafia-type organization based in Reggio Calabria, Italy. Founded in the 1980s by Pasquale Latella, it controls the Ravagnese and Croce Valanidi quarters and is allied with the Ficara, De Stefano, and Pelle 'ndrine. The clan has been involved in feuds and alliances, notably during the Second 'Ndrangheta war, and was investigated in 2013 for monopolizing the construction sector. It remains active.

The Latin Counts is an Indigenous Latino American street gang based in Chicago, Illinois, with a significant branch in Detroit, Michigan. Founded in 1955 by Tejano youth in the Pilsen neighborhood, it is a member of the People Nation alliance. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, racketeering, and other criminal activities.

The Latin Eagles are a Puerto Rican street gang founded in Chicago, Illinois in 1964. Originally formed as a club to protect against white greaser gangs, it evolved into a criminal organization. The gang is known for spawning the Young Lords political group in the late 1960s. They are aligned with the Folk Nation and have been active continuously since their founding.

nodes.description: The Latin Kings is a predominantly Hispanic street and prison gang founded in Chicago in 1954 by Puerto Ricans. It operates under two main factions: the King Motherland Chicago (KMC) and the Bloodline, with a total membership estimated between 22,000 and 42,500. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, assault, burglary, homicide, identity theft, and money laundering, with primary income from street-level narcotics distribution. It has a presence in 31 U.S. states and several other countries.

nodes.description: Early 20th-century New York City street gang based in Harlem, founded in the early 1900s by Harry Horowitz. It consisted mostly of pickpockets and burglars, allied with the Eastman Gang. The gang was involved in muggings, robberies, and murder, notably the assassination of gambler Herman Rosenthal in 1912. After the execution of its leaders in 1914, the gang disbanded.

It was one of the most important drug trafficking organizations in eastern Colombia, formed from the remnants of ERPAC. The group was led by Martín Farfán Díaz González, alias 'Pijarbey', and was completely dismantled after the capture of its last leader in September 2017.

The Libri 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a criminal organization in Calabria, Italy. Founded by brothers Domenico and Pasquale Libri in the 1950s, it is based in Reggio Calabria with a stronghold in the Cannavò district. The clan is involved in drug and arms trafficking, extortion, prostitution, and infiltration into public institutions. It reached its peak in the 1960s-1970s and remains active, considered one of the most aggressive 'ndrine in Reggio Calabria.

The Licciardi clan is a powerful Neapolitan Camorra clan based in Secondigliano, Naples, founded in the 1980s by Gennaro Licciardi. It controls drug trafficking and extortion in several Naples suburbs and is a founding member of the Secondigliano Alliance. The clan is currently led by Maria Licciardi, known as 'La Madrina', and remains active.

LockBit is a cybercriminal group that operates a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) model, first appearing on a Russian-language cybercrime forum in January 2020. The group encrypts victims' data and threatens to leak it publicly if ransoms are not paid. It was the most prolific ransomware in 2022, responsible for 44% of global ransomware incidents in early 2023. In February 2024, law enforcement seized its dark web sites, but the group continued attacks and attempted a comeback.

As of 2025, the group remains active with an estimated 12,000-20,000 members.

nodes.description: Los Ciclones, also known as the Facción Matamoros, is a Mexican criminal organization and one of the four main factions of the Gulf Cartel. Based in Matamoros, Tamaulipas, it was founded between 2010 and 2012 by Rafael Cárdenas Vélez. The group is engaged in drug trafficking, murder, kidnapping, extortion, and money laundering, and operates primarily in northeastern Mexico and the border area with Brownsville, Texas. It is currently active and in conflict with rival cartels such as the Cartel del Noreste and Los Metros.

nodes.description: Los Huistas are a powerful Guatemalan criminal organization based in Huehuetenango, near the Mexican border. Founded in the late 1990s, they control a strategic drug trafficking route for cocaine, methamphetamine, and heroin from Central America to the United States. They have evolved from transporters to producers of methamphetamine and money launderers, infiltrating state institutions. The group maintains a centralized hierarchy and is led by Eugenio Darío Molina-López until his capture in 2026.

It remains active and is allied with the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the Gulf Cartel.

Its members are mostly deportees or descendants of Mexicans, and leaving the gang is punishable by death.

nodes.description: Los Negros was the main armed wing of the Beltrán Leyva Cartel in Mexico, formed in 2003 to support the Sinaloa Cartel against the Gulf Cartel and Los Zetas. After the split between the Beltrán Leyva brothers and Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, Los Negros allied with Los Zetas. Led by Édgar Valdez Villarreal 'La Barbie', the group was involved in drug trafficking, murder, and extortion across multiple Mexican states. Following Valdez's capture in 2010, the group fragmented into independent cells.

nodes.description: Los Ninis are the main armed wing of the Los Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, composed of young hitmen aged 20-35 trained in urban combat. They operate as security forces for Los Chapitos leaders, and are involved in torture, murder, drug trafficking, and controlling cartel territories. Based in Culiacán, Sinaloa, they were formed to maintain Los Chapitos' dominance over the Sinaloa Cartel.

nodes.description: Colombian criminal and narcoparamilitary organization based in Medellín, formed in 2008 from remnants of paramilitary groups demobilized during peace talks (2004-2006). It was founded by former members of the Oficina de Envigado after the extradition of Don Berna. The group engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, kidnapping, and murder. It was dissolved by Colombian security forces in 2014, with remaining members joining the Clan Úsuga.

nodes.description: Los Pelones is an enforcer gang originally part of the Sinaloa Cartel, founded in 2004 in Guerrero, Mexico. It distributed narcotics in tourist spots and later became independent after the Beltrán-Leyva split. The group allied with the Gulf Cartel in 2012 and later became independent again due to fragmentation. It is involved in drug trafficking, murder, and extortion.

Colombian paramilitary group formed in 1992 to fight Pablo Escobar and the Medellín Cartel. Financed by the Cali Cartel and led by the Castaño brothers, they waged a small-scale war involving assassinations and bombings. The group disbanded after Escobar's death in 1993, with many members later joining the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC).

Colombian criminal group affiliated with the Medellín Cartel, active in the 1980s and early 1990s. The group was dismantled in 1991 when its leaders were killed by police.

nodes.description: Los Solidos is a street gang founded in the early 1990s by Lawrence Beauvais in Hartford, Connecticut. nodes.description: The Maceo Organization was a criminal syndicate that controlled Galveston, Texas, from the 1920s to the 1980s. Founded by brothers Sam and Rosario Maceo, it engaged in illegal gambling, prostitution, bootlegging, and racketeering. The organization wielded significant political influence, with ties to Texas Governor James V. Allred and other officials. It was eventually succeeded by the Fertitta Organization.

Mafia Capitale is an organized crime organization based in Rome, Italy, founded in 1999 by Massimo Carminati and Salvatore Buzzi. It engaged in money laundering, racketeering, political corruption, and bid rigging, stealing funds from city services. The organization was dismantled following a major investigation in 2014, and in 2020 Italy's Supreme Court ruled that its acts did not constitute mafia association.

nodes.description: The Mallardo clan is a Camorra crime clan based in Giugliano, Campania, Italy, founded in the late 1970s by Francesco Mallardo. It is a key member of the Secondigliano Alliance, considered the most powerful active Camorra group. The clan is involved in racketeering, smuggling, extortion, and drug trafficking, and has dominated the Neapolitan underworld since the 1990s. In 2011, Italian police seized assets worth €600 million from the clan.

The Mamak Gang is a notorious Malaysian gang active since the early 1990s, specializing in carjacking and robberies. They are most infamous for stealing RM 12 million worth of gold bars from the Malaysia Airlines cargo complex in 1994. Despite multiple arrests and preventive detention, they continued operations from prison until their last three members were arrested in December 2006.

A powerful clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Castellace and Oppido Mamertina in the Gioia Tauro plain, Calabria, Italy. Founded in the 1930s, it is involved in racketeering, kidnapping, and extortion. The clan is closely linked to the Rugolo clan through intermarriage and has been involved in a long feud with the Barbaro clan. It remains active.
