nodes.description: The Mancuso 'ndrina is a powerful clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in Limbadi and Nicotera, Calabria, Italy. Founded in the 1970s, it is considered the most influential clan in the province of Vibo Valentia and one of the most financially powerful in Europe. The clan is heavily involved in international cocaine trafficking, with operations extending to Africa, and also engages in extortion, usury, public procurement fraud, and money laundering. It maintains alliances with other 'Ndrangheta clans and has historical ties with Colombian and Colombian paramilitary groups.

nodes.description: The March 23 Movement (M23) is a Congolese rebel paramilitary group backed by Rwanda, based in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. It was founded in 2012 by former members of the National Congress for the Defence of the People (CNDP) who mutinied against the government. M23 captured Goma in 2012 but withdrew after negotiations, and resumed operations in 2022. It is the principal member of the Congo River Alliance.

nodes.description: The Marginals, also known as the Paddy Irish gang, was a New York street gang active in the early 1900s. Based on the Lower West Side of Manhattan, they were involved in extortion and labor slugging. Under leader Thomas F. 'Tanner' Smith, they succeeded the Hudson Dusters in their territory. The gang's reign ended with Smith's murder in 1919.

Marielitos are Cuban immigrants who arrived in the United States during the 1980 Mariel boatlift, with a subset involved in organized crime. They are based in the United States, primarily Miami, and are known for drug and arms trafficking, gambling, and contract killing. The group emerged in the early 1980s and remains active, with alliances with the American Mafia and other cartels.

nodes.description: The Market Street Commandos was an outlaw motorcycle club that participated in the 1947 Hollister incident alongside the Boozefighters and Pissed Off Bastards of Bloomington. The club merged with the Hells Angels in 1954 to become their San Francisco chapter.

The Markham Gang was a 19th-century criminal organization based in Ontario, Canada, evolving from groups supporting the Upper Canada Rebellion of 1837. It engaged in petty theft and counterfeiting, using a courier network to transport stolen goods. The gang was broken up in 1846, with members imprisoned but later released.

nodes.description: The Matsuba-kai is a yakuza organization based in Tokyo, Japan, founded in March 1953 from remnants of the Sekine-gumi and Fujita-gumi. The group is a member of the Kantō Hatsuka-kai federation and has been involved in drug smuggling, violent feuds, and protests.

The gang was active until around 1962.

The Mazzarella clan is a powerful Camorra organization based in Naples, Italy, founded in the 1960s by the Mazzarella brothers. Initially involved in cigarette smuggling, it grew into a major criminal group engaged in drug trafficking, money laundering, and other illicit activities. The clan has been involved in violent conflicts with rival Camorra clans and has international connections with the Sicilian Mafia and South American cartels. nodes.description: The Milwaukee crime family was an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, founded around 1918 by Vito Guardalabene. The Mullen Gang was an Irish-American street gang operating in South Boston, Massachusetts, founded in the 1950s. Engaged in racketeering, armed robbery, auto theft, and burglary, it fought a decade-long war with the Killeen Gang for control of criminal rackets. In 1972, both gangs were consolidated under the Winter Hill Gang. The gang derived its name from a commemorative plaque to war hero John Joseph Mullen.

Mungiki is a banned ethnic organization in Kenya, originating in the late 1980s among Kikuyu youth. The group is secretive and operates through a cell structure, with a reported peak membership of 500,000. It was banned by the Kenyan government.

Murder, Inc. was an organized crime group active from 1929 to 1941 that served as the enforcement arm of the National Crime Syndicate. Composed of Jewish-American and Italian-American gangsters, it was based in New York City and responsible for hundreds of contract killings. The Musitano crime family is a 'Ndrangheta organized crime family based in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, with branches in Italy. Founded by Angelo Musitano in the 1940s, it engaged in racketeering, drug trafficking, and murder. Key members Angelo and Pat Musitano were killed in 2017 and 2020, respectively.

nodes.description: Mexican criminal organization based in Jalisco, formed in 2018 as a split from the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. It operates primarily in the Guadalajara metropolitan area and disputes territory with CJNG. The group is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, robbery, murder, and arms trafficking, and has received funding from the Sinaloa Cartel. Its founding leaders were Érick Valencia Salazar, Emilio Alejandro Pulido Saldaña, and Carlos Enrique Sánchez Martínez.

The Numbers Gang is a South African prison-based criminal organization founded in the late 1800s in KwaZulu-Natal. It operates through three main factions: the 26s (smuggling), 27s (enforcement), and 28s (protection). The gang is known for its complex rules, internal hierarchy, and secretive nature, and traditionally does not operate outside of prisons.

Italian Camorra criminal organization founded in the late 1970s by Raffaele Cutolo in Campania. It was a structured, hierarchical organization that became the strongest Camorra clan by 1981, providing a living for at least 200,000 people in the Neapolitan area. It was hostile to the Sicilian Mafia but allied with 'Ndrangheta clans. The organization was considered extinct in the late 1980s after many members were killed or imprisoned.

The Nuova camorra pugliese was a criminal organization based in Apulia, Italy, active from the early 1970s to the mid-1980s. It was founded by Raffaele Cutolo as an offshoot of the Nuova Camorra Organizzata. The group operated mainly in the provinces of Foggia and Taranto. It was eventually absorbed by the Sacra corona unita.

The Nuova Famiglia was an Italian Camorra confederation created in the late 1970s to oppose Raffaele Cutolo's Nuova Camorra Organizzata. It was headed by powerful Camorra bosses including Carmine Alfieri, the Nuvoletta brothers, Michele Zaza, Luigi Giuliano, and Antonio Bardellino. The organization was active primarily in Campania and had ties with the Sicilian Mafia. It engaged in various criminal activities such as drug trafficking, murder, and extortion until its dissolution in the 1990s.

The group is considered by Italian authorities to have all characteristics of a mafia organization under Article 416 bis-cp. Founded in the 1960s by Lorenzo and Angelo Nuvoletta, it was affiliated with Sicilian Mafia families and considered one of the most powerful Camorra clans between the 1970s and 1990s. nodes.description: The Oaxaca Cartel was a smaller Mexican drug cartel operating in southern Mexico, particularly in Oaxaca and Chiapas. It focused on marijuana and cocaine trafficking and was allied with the Tijuana Cartel. Founded by Pedro Díaz Parada in the 1970s, the cartel was led by the Díaz-Parada brothers. The Obshchak is a traditional umbrella organization of criminal groups in Estonia, functioning as a trade union that settles conflicts and establishes boundaries among groups like the Russian mafia and Estonian organized crime. It pays for lawyers, delivers packages to imprisoned members, and covers other expenses. Dominated by Nikolai Tarankov from 2003 until his murder in 2016, the organization has about ten member groups and has been involved in drug trafficking, tax fraud, and violent crimes. Estonian police have disrupted its operations by arresting high-ranking members since the 2010s.

nodes.description: The Oda-gumi is a yakuza organization founded in 1958 by Hideomi 'Joji' Oda in Osaka, Japan. It operates as a subsidiary of the Yamaguchi-gumi syndicate. The group has been involved in internal conflicts and leadership disputes, and has faced legal issues including arrests of its leaders. As of 2021, its future is uncertain due to leadership demotions and ongoing troubles.

Originally founded as an enforcement wing and debt collection service for Pablo Escobar's Medellín Cartel, Oficina de Envigado evolved into a major drug cartel and criminal organization based in Medellín and Envigado, Colombia. It controls extortion, gambling, and money laundering in the Valle de Aburrá and acts as a mediator and debt collector in drug trafficking disputes. By 2019, its activities shifted from direct drug trafficking to providing services to lower-level traffickers and mafia groups. It maintains connections with Colombian paramilitaries and guerrillas.

Organised crime in India encompasses various criminal groups operating across the country and internationally, involved in activities such as smuggling, extortion, drug trafficking, and contract killing. The Mumbai underworld has been historically dominated by figures like Haji Mastan, Varadarajan Mudaliar, and Karim Lala. These groups have expanded their operations to countries including Canada, the United States, and the United Kingdom. The structure and leadership of Indian organized crime do not strictly follow the classical Sicilian Mafia model.

Notable groups include Area Boys in Lagos and confraternities like the Neo Black Movement of Africa. The organizations are involved in scams, drug trafficking, human smuggling, and other illicit activities.

nodes.description: The Papalia crime family is a 'Ndrangheta organized crime family based in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, founded by Antonio Papalia in the 1940s. It is one of three centralized Mafia organizations in Hamilton, with strong connections to the Buffalo crime family. The family was decimated after the killings of boss Johnny Papalia and his lieutenant in 1997, ordered by the Musitano family. The last leader, Frank Papalia, died in 2014.

nodes.description: The Parisi-Palermiti clan is a criminal organization originating from Bari, Italy, with its stronghold in the Japigia neighborhood. Founded in the 1980s by Savino Parisi and Eugenio Palermiti, it controls drug trafficking, extortion, and other illegal activities. The clan has infiltrated businesses and local politics, and has been involved in conflicts with rival groups. Despite the imprisonment of its founder, the organization remains active under the leadership of Eugenio Palermiti.

As of 2024, it has approximately 30 made members.

nodes.description: The PDC was a street gang based in Brixton, London, England, primarily active in the 1990s. They were involved in drug trafficking, robberies, and violence, and were the largest gang in the SW9 postcode. The gang later reformed as a music collective and label, while a faction broke off to form the 'Muslim Boys'.

The Peaky Blinders were a street gang based in Birmingham, England, operating from the 1880s until the 1920s. They engaged in robbery, violence, racketeering, illegal bookmaking, and gambling control. The gang was known for their distinctive attire and held dominance in Birmingham until being overtaken by the Birmingham Boys in 1920.

It operated mainly in Antioquia and Córdoba departments, protecting members' farms and drug interests while eliminating left-wing sympathizers. It later became the core of the United Self-Defenders of Colombia (AUC).

nodes.description: Multi-generational gang based in Peckham, South London, founded in the 1990s. Known for popularising road rap music and involvement in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, robbery, and murder. The gang operates in Peckham, Walworth, and Camberwell, and is divided into subsets by age group. Active as of 2025.

The Pelle 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta based in San Luca, Calabria, Italy, founded in the 1970s by Antonio Pelle. It is one of the most influential 'ndrine, involved in international cocaine trafficking, extortion, and contract rigging. The clan has members in the 'Ndrangheta's top management bodies and maintains a presence in Lombardy. It has been implicated in corrupting regional elections and has ongoing rivalries with the Nirta-Strangio clan.

nodes.description: The Penny Mobs was a street gang active in Glasgow, Scotland during the early 1870s. The name derived from the practice of collecting a penny per member to pay court fines, avoiding imprisonment. Formed by Irish immigrants fleeing the potato famines, the gang declined after courts stopped offering fines as an alternative to imprisonment.

The People Nation is an American alliance of street gangs based in Chicago, founded in 1978 by leaders of the Vice Lords, Black P. Stones, and Latin Kings. It is a multiethnic coalition involved in drug trafficking, robbery, money laundering, and murder. The alliance is known for its rivalry with the Folk Nation and uses symbols such as a five-pointed star and left-sided identifiers.

nodes.description: The People's Aman Committee was a Pakistani political party-affiliated militant group and organized crime gang based in Lyari, Karachi, founded in 2008 by Rehman Dakait. It engaged in drug trafficking, extortion, and gang wars, supporting the Pakistan People's Party. The group was officially banned in 2011 but continued de facto operations until the late 2010s.

nodes.description: The Pesce 'ndrina is a powerful clan of the 'Ndrangheta, based in Rosarno, Calabria, Italy. Founded in the 1950s by Giuseppe Pesce, it transformed from a rural criminal group into an entrepreneurial organization involved in drug trafficking, extortion, and control of commercial businesses in the Gioia Tauro plain. The clan has been led by Antonino and Salvatore Pesce, both currently imprisoned, with Francesco Pesce taking command. It remains active and influential.

The Petit Bar Gang is a Corsican organized crime group named after a bar in Ajaccio. It engages in extortion, money laundering, and other criminal activities, with influence in Corsica, mainland France, and abroad. Considered the most powerful criminal group in Corsica as of 2022, it has established political and economic networks. The group was founded in the 2000s and remains active.

nodes.description: The Pettingill family is a Melbourne-based criminal family headed by matriarch Kath Pettingill. Members have convictions for drug trafficking, arms dealing, and armed robberies. The family was involved in the 1988 Walsh Street police shootings and the Melbourne gangland killings, suffering a major blow with the murder of Victor Peirce. Their power has been greatly weakened since.

Italian American Mafia crime family based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, founded around 1911 by Salvatore Sabella. It operates throughout the Greater Philadelphia metropolitan area and South Jersey, known for violence and internal conflicts. The family experienced a peaceful era under Angelo Bruno (1959-1980) before a series of violent successions and wars. Currently active, with membership estimated at 50 made members and 100 associates as of 2004.

nodes.description: The Philadelphia Greek Mob was a loose-knit Greek-American criminal faction operating in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, closely allied with the Italian-American Philadelphia crime family. Active primarily from the 1970s to the 1980s, it engaged in racketeering, drug trafficking, extortion, loansharking, and illegal gambling. The group was led by Chelsais "Steve" Bouras until his assassination in 1981, after which its influence declined.

The Pietraperzia Mafia family is a crime family of the Sicilian Cosa Nostra based in Pietraperzia, a town in the province of Enna. It has deep historical roots dating back to at least 1900 and reemerged in the 1980s after a period of inactivity. The family is a close ally of the powerful Catania Mafia family and was involved in high-level mafia operations, including preparatory meetings for the 1992 Capaci bombing. It is currently active.

Boston-based Chinese criminal organization founded in the 1970s by Stephen 'Sky Dragon' Tse, who had ties to the 14K Triad. It engaged in drug trafficking, arms trafficking, fraud, prostitution, human trafficking, illegal gambling, money laundering, extortion, murder, illegal immigration, and racketeering. The group declined after Tse's imprisonment in the 1980s and was linked to the Boston Chinatown massacre.

The Piromalli 'ndrina is a powerful clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a mafia-type organization in Calabria, Italy. Based in Gioia Tauro, it rose to prominence under brothers Mommo and Giuseppe Piromalli in the 1960s. The clan has been involved in feuds and political corruption, and remains active with over 200 members.

The Pirus are a subset of the Bloods gang alliance, founded in 1969 in Compton, California by Sylvester Scott and Vincent Owens. They emerged as rivals to the Crips and are involved in drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. The gang remains active and influential in Los Angeles street gang culture.

The Piserà 'ndrina is a clan of the 'Ndrangheta, a criminal organization based in Tropea, Calabria, Italy. Active since the 1980s, it is allied with the Mancuso 'ndrina and has been in a feud with the La Rosa 'ndrina since the 1990s. The clan has been involved in violence, including the killing of municipal councilor Pasquale Piserà in 1982.

An outlaw motorcycle club founded in Bloomington, California in 1945 by Norman Briggs. The club participated in the 1947 Hollister riot, which inspired the film The Wild One. It is considered a precursor to the Hells Angels, as a former member founded that club. The club remains active in California, Nevada, and Utah.

The Pittsburgh crime family, also known as the LaRocca crime family, was an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Formed in the late 1880s under Salvatore Catanzaro, it rose to prominence during Prohibition and was led for decades by Sebastian LaRocca. The family engaged in racketeering, labor union infiltration, and drug trafficking, but became defunct after convictions and attrition, with the last known member dying in 2021.

nodes.description: The Plug Uglies were an American Nativist criminal street gang active in Baltimore, Maryland from 1854 to 1865. They were known for their involvement in election-day violence and street brawls, often using plug hats stuffed with wool as helmets. The gang participated in the 1856 Baltimore Know-Nothing Riot and the 1863 New York City Draft Riots. They were allied with the Know Nothing political party and rivaled Irish American gangs.

Polish-American organized crime refers to criminal groups composed of Polish immigrants and Polish Americans operating primarily in the United States. Active since the 1920s, these groups have been involved in bootlegging, drug trafficking, racketeering, and other illegal activities. Notable factions include the Kielbasa Posse in Philadelphia and the Greenpoint Crew in New York. They have historically allied with the Chicago Outfit and rivaled Irish and Russian mobs.

nodes.description: The Polverino clan is a Neapolitan Camorra clan based in Marano di Napoli, Italy, founded by Giuseppe Polverino in the 1990s. It emerged as a ramification of the Nuvoletta clan and became independent, known for monopolizing hashish importation from Morocco to Italy via Spain. The clan operates in various Italian regions and has a strong presence in Spain, particularly in Barcelona, Málaga, and Alicante. It is considered one of the most powerful Camorra groups in Spain.

nodes.description: The Potashes were a 19th-century Irish-American street gang active in Greenwich Village and the New York waterfront during the early to mid-1890s. Led by Red Shay Meehan, the gang was based near the Babbit Soap Factory on Washington Street. They terrorized the neighborhood and dominated Lower West Side Manhattan until the end of the 1890s, when they were displaced by the Hudson Dusters.

Preman is a term for Indonesian organized crime groups, encompassing street-level criminals to crime bosses. The word originates from the Dutch 'vrijman' (free man) and describes the confluence of state power and criminality. Premans are often perceived negatively due to associations with violence, but have historically acted as enforcers for local authorities. The related jago or jawara figure is romanticized as a champion of the people.

Brazilian organized crime syndicate founded in 1993 by eight prisoners at Taubaté Penitentiary. Based in São Paulo, it is Latin America's largest drug gang with 40,000 lifetime members and 60,000 contractors. Active throughout South America, West Africa, and Europe, it controls over 50% of Brazil's drug exports to Europe and has a partnership with the 'Ndrangheta. Known for a business model favoring quiet market expansion over violent turf wars.

nodes.description: The Pruszków mafia was a Polish criminal organization originating from Pruszków in the 1990s, active in the Warsaw area. It engaged in car theft, drug trafficking, kidnapping, extortion, weapon trafficking, and murder. Law enforcement dealt a severe blow in 2000 after a key member became a crown witness, and the group has not been significantly active since.

Public Enemy No. 1 (PEN1) is a street gang with prison presence formed in Long Beach, California, in the 1980s. Based in Orange County, it engages in identity theft, credit card fraud, and methamphetamine trafficking. The gang has ties to the Aryan Brotherhood and Nazi Lowriders. As of 2004, it had around 200 members statewide, with an estimated 400-500 members currently.

The Puccio family was an Argentine criminal family active in the early 1980s, based in San Isidro, Buenos Aires. The family, led by father Arquímedes Puccio, was convicted of four kidnappings and three murders. They targeted wealthy individuals for ransom, often killing victims despite payment. The family was arrested in 1985 after a police raid freed their last victim.

Mexican criminal group active in Michoacán, founded in 2021 as a self-defense group for avocado farmers but degenerated into a criminal racketeering organization. Possibly tied to La Resistencia. Led by José Artemio Maldonado, a major fuel thief involved in the Tula prison break.

Puente 13 is a Sureño street gang based in La Puente, California, founded around 1953 as the Bridgetown Gentlemen. It is affiliated with the Mexican Mafia and known for drug trafficking, fraud, murder, and assault. The gang claims the entire city of La Puente and operates in the San Gabriel Valley.

Puro Tango Blast is a loose affiliation of regionally based street and prison gangs of primarily Hispanic men from major Texas cities. Formed in the late 1980s within the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, it lacks a strict hierarchy and is classified as a security threat group. Members engage in drug trafficking, robbery, and other crimes. The organization remains active with an estimated 17,000–19,000 members.

The Purple Gang was a Jewish-American criminal mob based in Detroit, Michigan, during the Prohibition era. They engaged in bootlegging, hijacking, extortion, and murder, becoming Detroit's dominant criminal gang in the 1920s. The gang was led by the Bernstein brothers and was known for its violence. Internal strife and infighting led to its collapse in the early 1930s.

nodes.description: The Ramacca Mafia family is a crime family of the Sicilian Cosa Nostra, operating primarily in the town of Ramacca, Sicily. Founded in the 1950s by Calogero 'Liddu' Conti, it engages in extortion, infiltration of public contracts, and political influence. The family has maintained control over local economic interests and alliances with powerful neighboring families. It remains active, with recent leadership transitions and ongoing criminal operations.

The Ramashish Koeri gang was a caste-based dacoit band active in the Kaimur plateau region of Bihar, India, during the 1980s. Led by Ramashish Koeri after the death of previous leader Mohan Bind, the gang was responsible for over a hundred murders in the region. It emerged from a context of extreme poverty and feudal repression by Rajput landlords, with members from Scheduled Castes and backward castes. The gang's activities declined after the death of Ramashish Koeri, but it was succeeded by leaders like Kameswar Koeri.

nodes.description: The Savage Nomads were a mostly Puerto Rican and African American street gang founded in the South Bronx, New York City in 1970 by Benjamin Melendez. Active primarily in the 1970s, the gang engaged in small crimes and battles with rival gangs such as the Seven Immortals and Savage Skulls. After a period of dormancy, the gang resurfaced in 2017 with homicides linked to them.

The Savage Skulls are a mostly Puerto Rican and African American street gang founded in the Hunts Point area of the Bronx, New York, in the late 1960s. They gained popularity in the 1970s and declared war on drug dealers in Hunts Point. The gang was involved in conflicts with rival gangs and appropriated Nazi symbolism. They were featured in a 1979 documentary film.

The Scarface gang was a criminal gang possibly from the Netherlands, active in the 2000s and early 2010s. It consisted of two to six men and sometimes a woman, responsible for a series of violent armed robberies in Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, and France. The gang was named after the character Tony Montana from the film Scarface. Four members were arrested in December 2011, while two fled to Morocco and one disappeared.

nodes.description: The Shapiro Brothers were a group of Jewish-American mobsters from New York City, based in Williamsburg, who led a faction in the garment industry. They were involved in a violent conflict with Jacob Shapiro and Louis Buchalter for control of the industry in Brooklyn. All three brothers were killed by rivals between 1931 and 1934.

Gangs of Irish immigrants active in Bytown (later Ottawa) during the 1830s. nodes.description: Far-left political party and guerrilla group in Peru, founded in 1969 by Abimael Guzmán. It launched a 'people's war' in 1980 aiming to overthrow the government and establish a New Democracy through guerrilla warfare. The group is designated as a terrorist organization by Peru, the US, EU, Japan, and Canada. Since the capture of its leaders in the 1990s and 2012, its activity has declined, with remaining factions operating in the VRAEM region.

The Shinwa-kai is a yakuza group based in Takamatsu, Kagawa, Japan, with an estimated 30 active members. It was renamed from the Takamatsu Shinwa-kai in 1971 and registered as a designated yakuza group in December 1992. It is the only designated yakuza group based in the Shikoku region and has been a member of the anti-Yamaguchi federation Gosha-kai since 1996.

The Shirt Tails were a mid-19th-century street gang based in the Five Points slum in Manhattan, New York City. They wore their shirts outside their pants as insignia and concealed weapons beneath. Active from the 1830s to the 1860s, they participated in the New York Draft Riots and disappeared shortly before the American Civil War.

Created as a reaction to the control of the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), it has been in conflict with the PCC and other rival factions. The group remains active.

nodes.description: Sio Sam Ong is a leading Chinese triad in Malaysia, based in Penang and Selangor, with strong presence in northern states like Kedah and Perlis. Established in the 1940s-1950s, it is considered one of the most powerful triads in the country, primarily composed of Hokkien ethnic group. The organization is involved in international drug trafficking, kidnapping, murder, extortion, racketeering, and loansharking, and has been linked to multiple murders in Penang in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

nodes.description: A prominent street gang in New York's Fourth Ward during the late 1880s to the mid-1990s, known for violent muggings and murder. They lured victims into dive bars or used a bucket of ash to blind them before robbing and sometimes killing them. The gang was led by George Leese, a river pirate and illegal prize fight organizer. They dominated the Fourth Ward until police drove them out after the American Civil War.

The Slovak mafia comprises various organized crime groups in Slovakia, primarily controlled by Slovak interests. It emerged after the 1989 revolutions and became well-established in the 1990s, with activities including racketeering, drug trafficking, and political corruption. The groups are traditionally active in security, construction, and nightclub ownership. As of the 2010s, the traditional mafia structure is said to be gone, but smaller drug gangs and criminal networks persist.

Chinese gangs based in Fujian province that smuggle people to wealthier Western countries and regions. They use stolen passports, bribes, and fake business delegations to bypass immigration controls. Notable members include Cheng Chui Ping and Guo Liang Chi, who was involved in the Golden Venture incident. Active since the 1990s.

The Soai-kai is a yakuza organization based in Chiba, Japan, formed in 1945 by Toramatsu Takahashi. Originally an affiliate of the Sasada-ikka, it became independent in 1955. It is a designated yakuza group with an estimated 80 active members and is one of the three dominating yakuza groups in Chiba Prefecture.

The Società di Polistena is a 'ndrangheta criminal organization based in Polistena, Calabria, Italy, with influence in surrounding towns. It has been active since the late 19th century, with early recorded bosses including Pasquale Ferrara and Francesco Sergio. The group engaged in drug and arms trafficking, and was involved in reconstruction profiteering after the 1905 earthquake. It remains active, with historical ties to the Guerrisi and Mercuri families.

The Società foggiana is a mafia-type criminal cartel operating in Foggia and its province, with infiltrations in other Italian regions. It emerged in the early 1980s as a splinter of Raffaele Cutolo's Nuova Camorra Organizzata and gained recognition in 1994. Known for its brutality, it lacks a single leader but is organized into family-based 'batteries' with a federal structure. It is considered one of the most violent Italian mafias.

nodes.description: A large white supremacist prison gang in the United States, founded in 1997 by Tracy David 'Tinman' Swena in Utah. The gang operates both inside and outside prison walls, engaging in drug trafficking, extortion, and violence. It has a paramilitary ranking structure and requires members to attack sex offenders and informants. The SAC has expanded across multiple states and the federal prison system.

nodes.description: An outlaw motorcycle club formed in Tijuana, Mexico in 1959. The club's insignia is a chopper-style motorcycle. It conducts an annual charity run delivering toys to poor children in Tijuana.

The Somali Outlaws are a Somali American street gang based in the Minneapolis–Saint Paul metropolitan area, active since the 2000s. The gang operates primarily around the Karmel Mall in south Minneapolis and the Cedar-Riverside neighborhood, with additional territory in Saint Paul and Nashville. Their activities include drug trafficking and human trafficking. The gang's leader, Mustafa Ali, was killed in 2019.

Death squad based in El Salvador, composed mainly of police and military personnel acting as vigilantes targeting criminals and gang members. Active since around December 1994, it was dismantled in 1996 but resurfaced in 2014. Known for targeting Mara Salvatrucha and Mara 18 gangs, often leaving victims blindfolded and shot in the head.

The Sonora Cartel was a Mexican drug trafficking organization founded in 1987 by Miguel Caro Quintero and Rafael Caro Quintero, operating primarily in northern Mexico and the southwestern United States. It was considered one of the oldest and best-established cartels by the DEA, with direct links to Colombian cartels. The cartel was acquired by the Sinaloa Cartel by 2007 and reported defunct by 2010.

country_links.evidence_quote: The Sonora Cartel is believed to be one of the earliest cartels to begin shipping cocaine from Colombia , particularly from the Cali Cartel .

nodes.description: Crips-affiliated street gang based in Long Beach, California, founded by the 1980s. Membership primarily consists of Samoan Americans and other Pacific Islanders. Involved in drug trafficking, robbery, burglary, and extortion. Operates in multiple U.S. states including Alaska, California, Missouri, Utah, and Washington.

One percenter outlaw motorcycle club based in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, founded in 1949 by returning WWII veterans. Originally a family-oriented club, it became a violent gang under John 'Satan' Marron, who later became National President of the Pagan's Motorcycle Club. The club is a brother club to the Pagans and wears a diamond 'P' patch to signify allegiance. Its clubhouse was destroyed by a pipe bomb in 2002, suspected to be by Hells Angels.

nodes.description: The Spanish Cobras is a primarily Latino street gang founded in the 1970s in Chicago, Illinois, by former members of the Maniac Latin Disciples. It operates in multiple Midwestern states and has a strong presence on Chicago's north and west sides. The gang is part of the Folk Nation alliance and is known for its rivalry with People Nation gangs, including the Latin Kings.

The Spanish Gangster Disciples is an Indigenous Latino American street gang originating in South Chicago, founded by Rudy Rios in the early 1980s. It is an offshoot of the Gangster Disciples and is part of the Folk Nation alliance. The gang is involved in drug trafficking, assault, robbery, and murder, and remains active.

nodes.description: White racist youth gang based in South Gate, California, active from the 1940s to the 1950s. Formed in reaction to the growing African American population in Los Angeles, the gang opposed integration and racial segregation, starting fights and intimidating black youths. Their activities prompted the formation of black protective gangs such as the Slausons.

The St. Louis crime family was an Italian-American Mafia crime family based in St. Louis, Missouri, founded around the 1890s. It was involved in racketeering, gambling, drug trafficking, and other illegal activities. The family was active until approximately 2014, with ties to other Mafia families such as the Chicago Outfit and Detroit Partnership.

The State Line Mob was an association of criminal elements operating in the 1950s and 1960s along the Mississippi–Tennessee state line. Involved in bootlegging, gambling, prostitution, robbery, and murder, it owned motels, restaurants, and clubs that served as centers for vice. The group gained national attention for its feud with Sheriff Buford Pusser, which inspired the film Walking Tall.

The Stidda is a Sicilian Mafia-type criminal organization based in southern Sicily, founded in the early 1980s by former Cosa Nostra members expelled during the Second Mafia War. It operates primarily in rural areas and is known for its star tattoo. The Stidda engaged in a violent conflict with Cosa Nostra in the 1990s, resulting in over 300 deaths. It remains active, with an estimated 2,000 full members.

nodes.description: The Stopwatch Gang was a group of three Canadian bank robbers active from 1974 to 1980. They robbed over 140 banks in the United States and Canada, stealing approximately $15 million Canadian dollars. Known for meticulous planning and non-violent methods, they completed robberies in under two minutes. The gang was named by the FBI after a member wore a stopwatch during a heist.

country_links.context: The Stopwatch Gang robbed banks in the United States, including a gold heist at Ottawa airport (Canada) and many bank robberies along the California coast, with their biggest heist in San Diego.

nodes.description: The Straight Satans Motorcycle Club was a one-percenter outlaw motorcycle gang based in Southern California, founded in July 1959 by three bikers known as Father Bill, Little Jerry, and Glick. It was among the earliest outlaw motorcycle clubs in the Los Angeles area, but remained localized without chapters beyond its original base. The club gained notoriety for its association with the Manson Family during the late 1960s, particularly around the Tate–LaBianca murders. It was implicated in criminal incidents including a sexual assault in 1972.

nodes.description: The Strisciuglio clan is a powerful and violent criminal organization based in Bari, Italy, founded in the late 1990s by Domenico Strisciuglio. It operates primarily in the northern area of Bari, engaging in murder, drug trafficking, money laundering, extortion, usury, and gambling. The clan has close ties with local politics and is currently active.

The Suey Sing Association is a historical Chinese American association established in 1867. Formerly known as the Suey Sing Tong, it changed to its current name in 1920. In 1994, it became the first Chinese community organization to fly the flag of the People's Republic of China. It has branches across the United States and Canada with over 1000 members.

nodes.description: The Suishin-kai was a Japanese yakuza gang based in Nagasaki, affiliated with the Yamaguchi-gumi. It came to prominence in April 2007 when its former underboss, Tetsuya Shiroo, assassinated the mayor of Nagasaki, Iccho Itoh. The gang voluntarily disbanded shortly after the killing due to intense police scrutiny.

The Sumiyoshi-kai is the second-largest yakuza group in Japan, based in Tokyo. Founded in 1958 by Jusaku Abe, it operates as a confederation of smaller gangs with a loose chain of command. The group engages in protection rackets in upscale districts like Kabukichō and Ginza. As of 2020, it had an estimated 2,100 members.

Sun Yee On is one of the leading triads in Hong Kong and China, founded in 1919 by Heung Chin. It has over 25,000 members worldwide and is active in multiple countries including the UK, US, France, and Belgium. The triad is involved in racketeering, counterfeiting, extortion, drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and illegal gambling. It remains active as of the present day.

Specialized in crack cocaine distribution, generating over $200,000 daily at its 1987 peak. Known for extreme violence and murder to control drug trade. The Sureños are a Mexican-American street gang alliance originating in Southern California, founded in 1967. They are loosely organized with hundreds of individual gangs under the Sureño umbrella, primarily active in the southwestern United States and expanding to other regions. Their roots trace back to a prison rivalry between the Mexican Mafia and Nuestra Familia. They are involved in drug trafficking, murder, and organized crime, and maintain alliances with Mexican drug cartels.

nodes.description: The Swamp Angels were a New York City waterfront street gang active from the 1850s to the 1890s. Based in a rookery called Gotham Court on Cherry Street in Lower Manhattan, they used the sewers to raid East River dockyards and sell stolen cargo quickly. The gang was predominantly Irish and Irish-American. They eventually merged with rival gangs to form the White Hand Gang.

Street gang in Perth, Western Australia, consisting mostly of Lebanese Australians, known to authorities since the mid-1990s. Members wear a miniature gold scimitar necklace. Involved in amphetamine and ecstasy distribution, and linked to car rebirthing. Members were convicted in 2016 for drug trafficking.

The Sydney Ducks was a gang of criminal immigrants from Australia operating in San Francisco during the mid-19th century. They were blamed for an 1849 fire and rampant crime, leading to the formation of the first Committee of Vigilance in 1851. The vigilantes decimated the gang through lynchings and deportations. The area they clustered in became known as the Barbary Coast.

The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) is a Kurdish-led coalition of left-wing ethnic militias and rebel groups founded on 10 October 2015. It serves as the official military wing of the Democratic Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria (Rojava). The SDF aims to create a secular, democratic, and federalized Syria, and has been a key U.S. ally in fighting the Islamic State. It is opposed by Turkey, which views it as an extension of the PKK. In 2025, the SDF agreed to integrate into Syrian state institutions.

Syriac-Aramean criminal organization based in Södertälje, Sweden, founded in the early 1980s. It is structured around family and kinship ties, with no single leader. The group is involved in drug trafficking, murder, welfare fraud, extortion, and other crimes. It has been confirmed by Swedish courts and continues to grow.

The Taishu-kai is a yakuza organization based in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, with an estimated 60 active members. It was formed around 1954 by Kuniharu Ota as the Ota Group, later renamed Ota-gumi, and finally Taishu-kai in 1973. It is one of five independent Fukuoka-based designated yakuza syndicates and a member of the anti-Yamaguchi-gumi federation Yonsha-kai.

nodes.description: The Takumi-gumi is a Japanese yakuza syndicate based in the Kansai region, founded in 1967 by Masaru Takumi. It was originally part of the Yamaguchi-gumi, with Takumi serving as second-in-command. After Takumi's assassination in 1997, Tadashi Irie became the leader. The group withdrew from the Yamaguchi-gumi in 2015 to form the Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi, and later left that group in 2022. By 2023, membership had dwindled to about 20 members.

The Taliban is an Afghan political and militant organization that emerged in 1994 during the Second Afghan Civil War. Founded by Mullah Omar, it ruled most of Afghanistan from 1996 to 2001, enforcing a strict interpretation of sharia law. Overthrown by a US-led invasion in 2001, it waged a 20-year insurgency before recapturing Kabul in 2021 and now controls all of Afghanistan. The group is designated as a terrorist organization by several countries and is widely condemned for human rights abuses.

nodes.description: The Tanglewood Boys was an Italian-American recruitment gang or farm team for the Lucchese crime family, operating from the Tanglewood Shopping Center in Yonkers, New York. Active from the 1990s to the 2000s, the gang was involved in murders, assaults, armed robbery, arsons, and bookmaking in Westchester County, the Bronx, and the Upper West Side. Many members were sons of made men. The gang's downfall followed high-profile murders and subsequent prosecutions.

Arab American street gang formed in Chicago in 1992 to protect the Arab-American community from racially motivated assaults after the Gulf War. They disbanded in 1999 after losing members to rival gangs. Their colors were white and red, and their symbol was a four-pointed star.

The Taylor Street Jousters were a Chicago street gang originating in Little Italy, Chicago, in the 1950s or 1960s. They were primarily Italian and Mexican, known for their medieval knight symbols. The gang was allied with the Chicago Outfit and Gaylords, and rivaled the Gangster Disciples, Latin Kings, and Simon City Royals. They were active until 2005.

nodes.description: The Brotherhood of Eternal Love was an organization of drug users and distributors operating from the mid-1960s through the late 1970s in Orange County, California. Founded by John Griggs, it produced and distributed LSD and hashish with the goal of sparking a 'psychedelic revolution' in the United States. The group was known for the 'Orange Sunshine' LSD tablets and assisted Timothy Leary's escape from prison. Its activities largely ended after a 1972 drug raid, though some members were arrested as late as 2009.

The Carlton Crew is a criminal organization based in Melbourne, Australia, founded in the 1970s by Gino Rosace. It is named after the Melbourne suburb of Carlton and has been involved in racketeering, murder, drug trafficking, and other crimes. The group played a significant role in the Melbourne gangland killings and has been a rival to Calabrian 'Ndrangheta groups. As of 2019, Tony Madafferi is the boss.

The governing body of the American Mafia, formed in 1931 by Charles 'Lucky' Luciano after the Castellammarese War. It consists of the bosses of the Five Families of New York City, the Chicago Outfit, and occasionally other families. The Commission oversees Mafia activities in the United States and mediates conflicts between families. It was involved in the Apalachin meeting, a 1963 murder plot, and the 1985 Mafia Commission Trial.

Formed by Nicky Barnes in 1972, the seven-man organization handled local criminal disputes and drug distribution. It was heavily connected to the Italian-American Mafia, supplied by the Lucchese crime family. The Council dissolved in 1983 after Barnes became a federal informant.

nodes.description: Narcoterrorist organization created by Colombian drug lords in the early to mid 1980s to oppose extradition to the United States. Its members were largely drawn from the Medellín Cartel, led by Pablo Escobar. The group engaged in bombings, assassinations, and kidnappings to pressure the Colombian government. It was active from 1984 until Escobar's death in 1993.

The Family was an African-American organized crime group based in Newark, New Jersey, founded by Akbar Pray in the early 1970s. It was primarily involved in drug trafficking, particularly cocaine, and at its height had over 300 members. The group collapsed after Pray was sentenced to life in prison in 1990, becoming fragmented.

English organized crime group based in Bethnal Green, London, led by the Kray twins from the late 1950s until their arrest in 1968. Involved in murder, armed robbery, arson, protection rackets, gambling, and assaults. The twins were convicted in 1969 and sentenced to life imprisonment.

nodes.description: A group of Romanichal criminals from Cheltenham, Gloucestershire, who specialized in stealing fine art and antiques from English country houses over 20 years. The gang stole goods worth an estimated £30-80 million and were sentenced to a total of 49 years in prison in August 2008. Members included Ricky Johnson, his sons Richard and Albi, nephew Daniel O'Loughlin, and Michael Nicholls.

Founded by Robert Jay Mathews, the group raised funds through armed robbery and was involved in the murder of radio host Alan Berg. Inspired by The Turner Diaries, it aimed to overthrow the U.S. government and establish a white homeland. The group was dismantled after a shootout that killed Mathews.

nodes.description: The Westies were an Irish criminal gang based in Blanchardstown, west Dublin, Ireland. They controlled the heroin trade in west Dublin during the late 1990s and early 2000s, and were known for extreme violence against drug addicts and rival dealers. The gang also engaged in armed robberies and extortion. The organization imploded after the murders of all its leaders.

The Yiddishers were a London street gang based in Whitechapel, led by Alfred Solomon. Active during the inter-war years, they opposed the growing fascist movement in Great Britain and participated in the Battle of Cable Street in 1936. The gang included future mobster Jack Spot among its members.

nodes.description: An alliance of three ethnic armed groups in Myanmar: the Arakan Army, Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army, and Ta'ang National Liberation Army, formed in June 2019. It rose to prominence in 2023 by launching Operation 1027 against the Burmese junta following the 2021 coup. The alliance operates mainly in Rakhine State and northern Shan State, and remains active in the Myanmar civil war.

Thuggee was a phenomenon of highway robbery in the Indian subcontinent, where gangs of thugs murdered and robbed travelers, often by strangling. It gained prominence in the early 19th century during British colonial rule, and was portrayed as a secret fraternity of ritual stranglers. The colonial campaign against thuggee, led by William Henry Sleeman, resulted in thousands of convictions. Modern historians view thuggee as ordinary banditry rather than a religious cult.

nodes.description: The Toa-kai is a yakuza syndicate based in Tokyo, Japan, founded in 1948 by Zainichi Korean mob boss Hisayuki Machii as the Tosei-kai. Originally a far-right anti-communist organization, it became one of Tokyo's most powerful gangs during post-war economic growth. The group is a member of the Kanto Hatsuka-kai federation and has aligned with the Yamaguchi-gumi. As of the infobox, it has an estimated 20 members.

nodes.description: Tokuryū is a term coined by Japan's National Police Agency for loosely organized criminal groups that have emerged as an alternative to traditional yakuza. These groups are decentralized, rely on digital communication for recruitment and coordination, and engage in fraud, drug trafficking, robberies, and other crimes. They recruit young people through social media with promises of high earnings from 'dark part-time jobs'.

Japanese American gang founded in 1942 at Manzanar concentration camp during World War II. Initially formed by rebellious youths due to harsh internment conditions, the gang engaged in petty crimes like stealing rations. After release, members continued criminal activities in California, with membership growing post-internment. The gang was active until 1996.

The Tongan Crip Gang is a Tongan American street gang and a subset of the Crips alliance, founded in Inglewood, California. It is active in California, Utah, Alaska, Washington, and parts of Auckland, New Zealand. The gang engages in a wide range of criminal activities including drug trafficking, robbery, extortion, and murder. It was involved in a 2007 federal indictment for a conspiracy to murder members of MS-13.

nodes.description: Haitian paramilitary and secret police force created in 1959 by dictator François Duvalier. Formally disbanded in 1986, but members continued terrorizing the country.

nodes.description: Mexican-American street gang based in Atwater Village, Los Angeles County, founded in the 1930s. Engages in murder, assault, drug trafficking, racketeering, and other crimes. Allied with the Mexican Mafia and Sureños, and rivals several other gangs. Still active.

Japanese yakuza gang founded by Hisayuki Machii in 1948, based in Tokyo. It grew to over 1,500 members by the early 1960s and was known as the 'Ginza police'. The gang was involved in black market activities, strikebreaking, and alliances with other yakuza groups. Its current status is unclear.

nodes.description: Organised street gang based in Tottenham, North London, originating on the Broadwater Farm estate in the 1970s. Splintered into various groups by the mid-2000s.

The Trafficante crime family is an Italian American Mafia crime family based in Tampa, Florida, founded around 1920 by Ignacio Antinori. After his death in 1987, Vincent LoScalzo controlled the family until his death in 2025. The family is still active.

nodes.description: The Tribesmen are a prominent outlaw motorcycle club based in the North Island of New Zealand, founded in 1980 in Murupara. They are known for their yellow colors and middle finger salute, and have chapters in Ōtara, Northland, Rotorua, Murupara, and Christchurch. The club was one of the first organized groups to import and manufacture methamphetamine in New Zealand, but lost influence due to overindulgence in their own product. As of 2020, they are considered the dominant gang in Christchurch.

They also engage in human trafficking, illegal gambling, and extortion in Turkey and European countries with Turkish communities. Some members have ties to the Turkish deep state and far-right groups like the Grey Wolves.

It was part of the Consorzio, a drug cartel with Italian-Canadian families and Hells Angels. Current membership is estimated at 100-150, and the gang remains active under boss Gerald Matticks.

Known for being virulently anti-Italian and particularly violent, the gang suffered from unstable leadership and internal killings, leading to its demise.

nodes.description: Italian criminal organization active from 1987 to 1994, primarily in Emilia-Romagna and Marche. Composed largely of police officers with right-wing extremist ties, the gang committed 102 heists, resulting in 24 deaths and 102 injuries. Founded by the Savi brothers, it was known for using a white Fiat Uno. The gang was dismantled in 1994 after police investigations.

The Whitney gang was a family-based criminal organization from the Anfield district of Liverpool, England, active from the 1980s until 2011. They were involved in drug trafficking, specifically conspiracy to supply Class A drugs. In November 2011, members and associates were sentenced to a total of 82 years in prison. The gang was led by the Whitney family, including Carol, Leslie, Lisa, Paul, Anthony, and Gary Whitney.

The Whyos were a dominant street gang in New York City from the late 1860s to the early 1890s, formed from remnants of Five Points gangs after police crackdowns. They controlled much of Manhattan, engaging in street fighting, murder, robbery, and extortion. The gang was predominantly Irish and required members to have killed at least once. They were eventually defeated by the Monk Eastman Gang.

nodes.description: The Yamaken-gumi is a yakuza gang based in Kobe, Japan, founded in 1961 by Kenichi Yamamoto. It was the largest affiliate of the Yamaguchi-gumi until 2015, when it withdrew to form the Kobe Yamaguchi-gumi. After a period of independence, it rejoined the Yamaguchi-gumi in 2021. The group has an estimated membership of around 800.

The Yellow Henry Gang was a 19th-century New Orleans street gang active during the early 1870s and late 1880s. Originally led by Turpo, it was taken over by "Yellow" Henry Stewart after Turpo's arrest in 1877. The gang engaged in burglaries, armed robberies, and extortions, attracting many prominent criminals. It disbanded after leader Henry died in prison in 1886 and briefly reformed in 1888 before final dissolution in 1892.

Criminal organization and extortion ring operating on New York's Lower East Side in the early 20th century, led by Jacob 'Johnny' Levinsky. It targeted Jewish immigrant businessmen, particularly pushcart vendors and ice cream manufacturers, using anonymous threat letters. The group also engaged in assault, theft, and murder for hire.

Young Boys Inc. was a major African American drug organization based in Detroit, Michigan, founded in 1976 by Dwayne Davis, Bernard Boykins, Reginald Chestnut, and Charles Lindsey. It pioneered inner-city street-corner heroin sales using minors as couriers to avoid severe penalties. The group expanded to other cities like Boston and controlled up to 80% of Detroit's heroin trade until its leadership was indicted and convicted in 1982.

The Young Lords were a far-left political organization that evolved from a Chicago street gang founded in 1959. Known for direct action campaigns and community service programs, they advocated for Puerto Rican independence and socialism. Major branches existed in Chicago and New York City, with the New York chapter later becoming the Young Lords Party. The organization dissolved in 1972 due to internal splits and FBI counterintelligence operations.

country_links.context: The Young Lords Party expanded into Puerto Rico, transferring members and establishing a branch there.

nodes.description: The Yüksekova Gang was an illegal organization based in the Yüksekova district of Hakkari Province, Turkey, accused of killing 16 people. It had apparent links to the Turkish Gendarmerie's JITEM unit and possible links to the Ergenekon organization. The gang smuggled drugs and weapons, and its activities were first revealed in 1996 after the Susurluk scandal. Legal cases against the gang were sent to the European Court of Human Rights.

The clan is involved in drug trafficking, arms smuggling, extortion, and contract killings. Its leaders included Dušan Spasojević and Milorad Ulemek, and it had ties to Serbian state security services. nodes.description: The Ñetas are a criminal organization originally formed among inmates at Oso Blanco prison in Río Piedras, Puerto Rico, in 1979 by Carlos Torres Iriarte. Initially a mutual protection group, they evolved into a dominant prison gang involved in drug trafficking, robbery, and murder. They have expanded to the United States and Spain, with an estimated 7,000 members in Puerto Rico and 5,000 abroad. The group remains active and is known for its white color identification.

country_links.evidence_quote: In Spain, membership of the Ñetas is predominantly Ecuadorian. ... On May 11, 2014, a brawl occurred in Madrid involving Ñetas and Trinitarios which resulted in two injuries and the arrests of twenty-six gang members.
country_links.context: The Ñetas have a branch in Spain, predominantly composed of Ecuadorians, and have been involved in brawls with rival gangs.

descriptions: The Errol Flynns and 7 Mile Killers are mentioned as similar Detroit street gangs from the same era, but no direct relationship is stated.
edges.evidence_quote: Like other Detroit street gangs, such as their Westside Detroit counterparts in the late 1970s; the Nasty Flynns (later the NF Bangers), and 7 Mile Killers or 7 Mile Dogs or the drug consortiums of the 1980s such as Young Boys Inc., Pony Down, Best Friends, Black Mafia Family and the Chambers Brothers, the Errol Flynns grew out of the racial and economic unrest that transformed Detroit in the late 1960s and 1970s.

descriptions: The Errol Flynns are recognized as the precursors to these successor gangs.
edges.evidence_quote: Some of the most notable successors include the "Be Like Boys", "Dexter Boys" (an offshoot of YBI), "Schoolcraft Boys or SCB's", "SNS", "Fenkell Boys", "FMK" ("Fenkell Mafia Killers"), "7 Mile Killers or 7 Mile Dogs", "Linwood Boys", "Brewster Boys", "Jeffries Boys", and "8 Mile sconys", ("JBFL") "Joy Boys" or "Exit 9" All of these crews, excepting the "Be Like Boys" gang, are named after Detroit city streets or housing projects and some of these gangs still exist under new leadership.
